a100.speaker: Auditor General's report (Ghana)
a100.name: Auditor General's report (Ghana)
a100.speech: Source of the stories "Massive irregularities uncovered in public institutions", "MDAs exceed 2012 budget by GH¢1.23bn" and "Irregularities in use of public funds… Ghana loses GH¢4.2 billion".

a100.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a100.name: John Dramani Mahama
a100.title: President of Ghana
a100.speech: Justifying the withdrawal of allowances for trainee teachers, the President said its replacement with the Students Loan Trust Scheme had increased intake to the colleges of education from 9,000 to 15,000 in just a year of its introduction.

a100.speaker: Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT)
a100.name: Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT)
a100.speech: Did not agree with the withdrawal and asked for a review of the policy, arguing that if trainee teachers went for loans to finance their education in the colleges of education they couldn't be bonded by the Ghana Education Service (GES) after their graduation.

a100.speaker: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, then Minister of Education (current Vice-President)
a100.name: Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang
a100.title: then Minister of Education (current Vice-President)
a100.speech: Stated that her ministry had declared 2014 a year of zero tolerance for teacher absenteeism.

a223.speaker: Keaoleboga Dipogiso, University of Botswana (UB) political analyst
a223.name: Keaoleboga Dipogiso
a223.title: University of Botswana (UB) political analyst
a223.speech: Says there is a need for Masisi to make a reflection on the party's 2019 General Elections manifesto. "It is important for him to update the members on the progress they have made on issues of unemployment, diversification of the economy and the resentment of some within the BDP, especially regarding internal issues. He must tell the members what his central committee is intending to do in order to unify the party. Even if opposition parties are not organised to win the 2024 General Elections, the BDP has to be united also for them to win elections. They need each other in the coming election," Dipogiso said in an interview this week.

a392.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM) report, "A lifeline in danger"
a392.name: World Food Programme (WFP/PAM) report
a392.title: "A lifeline in danger"
a392.speech: Warned that cuts in humanitarian aid funding could expose up to 13.7 million people to extreme hunger worldwide: "The humanitarian aid system is under strong pressure with the withdrawal of partners from front-line areas, creating a vacuum." ; The UN agency said six of its operations - in Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan - are "facing major disruptions, which will only get worse"; warned its funding "has never been so challenging", anticipating "a 40% drop" in 2025, translating into a projected budget of $6.4 billion compared with $10 billion in 2024 ; "Programme coverage has been significantly reduced and rations cut. Vital assistance to families in food catastrophe situations [IPC Phase 5] is threatened, while preparedness for future shocks has significantly declined." ; "WFP estimates that its funding shortfalls could push 10.5 to 13.7 million people currently in acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3) into humanitarian emergency (IPC Phase 4)" ; Said global hunger has already reached record levels, with 319 million people facing acute food insecurity, including 44 million at emergency levels, that famine has hit Gaza and Sudan, and that in Afghanistan food assistance is reaching less than 10% of food-insecure people ; Says it expects to receive about $1.5 billion from the United States this year, down from nearly $4.5 billion last year, while other major donors have also cut funding.

a392.speaker: Study published in the medical journal The Lancet
a392.name: Study published in the medical journal The Lancet
a392.speech: Cited by the report as finding that 14 million additional deaths worldwide from disease, nutritional deficiencies and maternal and perinatal conditions could occur by 2030 as a result of cuts to US humanitarian aid alone.

a392.speaker: Lusa (news agency)
a392.name: Lusa (news agency)
a392.speech: Cited as the source of the report's contents, noting that the report does not name any country but points to the Lancet study.

a465.speaker: Malawi Law Society (statement released Thursday evening, co-signed by chairman Davis Njobvu and honorary secretary Francis M’mame)
a465.name: Malawi Law Society (statement released Thursday evening
a465.title: co-signed by chairman Davis Njobvu and honorary secretary Francis M’mame)
a465.speech: Described this as “not an isolated incident”. “Violence has repeatedly been unleashed against those who have sought to exercise their right to freedom of assembly and other allied rights, most of which has been in full view of the state machinery,” reads the statement. It adds: “The Society considers this inaction by the State and its security agents, which has in some instances been accompanied by cosmetic action, to be a calculated suppression of the right to freedom of assembly enshrined under section 38 of the Constitution of the Republic of Malawi.” ; Calls the incident “brutal, especially happening under the watch of the security agents”.

a465.speaker: Malawi Law Society (statement)
a465.name: Malawi Law Society (statement)
a465.speech: Asked President Lazarus Chakwera to sack Inspector General of Police Meryln Yolamu and Minister of Homeland Security Ezekiel Ching’oma following the brutal attacks on rights activists, journalists and protesters in Lilongwe on Thursday, saying the attacks raise serious questions about the competence and impartiality of the Inspector General and arguing that Yolamu and Ching’oma failed to motivate and direct their charges to control the situation ; “The Society notes that under Section 153(4) of the Constitution, the Minister is responsible for ensuring that the discipline and conduct of the Malawi Police Service accord with prescriptions of the Constitution, a responsibility that the Minister has demonstrably failed to uphold,” says the statement.

a465.speaker: Bishop Gilford Matonga, spokesperson for the Public Affairs Committee (PAC)
a465.name: Bishop Gilford Matonga
a465.title: spokesperson for the Public Affairs Committee (PAC)
a465.speech: Condemned the silence and inaction of the two security agencies, saying their inaction is disturbing and lends itself to the conclusion that these panga-wielding thugs are agents of some political authorities.

a465.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement released Friday)
a465.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement released Friday)
a465.speech: Condemned the Thursday brutalisation of protestors as “barbaric and cowardly”. “The brutality witnessed— ranging from the vicious assault on unarmed citizens to the burning of their vehicles— constitutes a grave violation of human rights and a blatant attack on Malawi’s democratic fabric. What is even more disturbing is that this heinous violence occurred in full view of the Malawi Police Service and Malawi Defence Forces, whose officers stood by and did nothing to protect innocent citizens,” it says. The body says it is “deeply outraged by this gross dereliction of duty” and describes the inaction of the security forces as “a betrayal of the public trust and a stain on [their] constitutional mandate.”

a465.speaker: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement)
a465.name: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) (statement)
a465.speech: “We wish to be absolutely clear: the pattern of selective enforcement and impunity for pro-government thugs suggests, beyond reasonable doubt, that these acts are being tolerated— if not orchestrated—by elements within the governing party. If the so-called ‘panga team’ had been affiliated with the opposition, we are convinced that arrests would have been swift and ruthless. The continued failure to bring these assailants to justice points directly to political protection from the highest levels of power in the governing party.” The religious body says it rejects the narrative that violence is justified simply because a demonstration may have been organised by opposition voices: “The government has a non-negotiable fiduciary obligation to ensure that security agencies act impartially and in the interest of all Malawians, not as instruments of intimidation for political gain.”

a465.speaker: Malawi Human Rights Commission (MHRC)
a465.name: Malawi Human Rights Commission (MHRC)
a465.speech: Said yesterday that the attacks on peaceful demonstrators are a serious threat to democracy, and said the silence from the police is making people lose trust in the system.

a465.speaker: Chikondi Chijozi, chairperson of the Malawi Human Rights Commission (MHRC)
a465.name: Chikondi Chijozi
a465.title: chairperson of the Malawi Human Rights Commission (MHRC)
a465.speech: Speaking at a press briefing in Lilongwe Friday, said police failed to protect the demonstrators even though the protest was legal.

a465.speaker: Bakili Muluzi, former President of Malawi
a465.name: Bakili Muluzi
a465.title: former President of Malawi
a465.speech: Described the harassment of protestors on Thursday as unacceptable, taking the police and the MDF to task, saying they are trained to protect and serve the public, not to enable violence or remain passive in the face of brutality, and that violence is “a grave affront to human dignity and the rule of law”, demanding accountability for the perpetrators ; “As a former Head of State, I am deeply concerned about the implications of this incident on our democracy and human rights record,” Muluzi said. He said Malawi’s security forces have a constitutional duty to protect citizens during peaceful assemblies, not to “stand idly by” while violence unfolds. “If the police were unable to protect the lives and property of demonstrators, what was their purpose for being there?” Muluzi questioned. “I urge relevant authorities to investigate both the attackers and the security forces’ inaction, and to ensure justice is served.”

a465.speaker: Civil society leaders, opposition political parties and others (at the Public Affairs Committee stakeholder conference in Blantyre)
a465.name: Civil society leaders
a465.title: opposition political parties and others (at the Public Affairs Committee stakeholder conference in Blantyre)
a465.speech: Demanded answers from the police why they had failed to make arrests in relation to previous incidences despite the thugs being known to them.

a465.speaker: Meryln Yolamu, Inspector General of the Malawi Police Service
a465.name: Meryln Yolamu
a465.title: Inspector General of the Malawi Police Service
a465.speech: In her response to some of the concerns, Yolamu said: “We investigated, some people were arrested and others are currently on bail. And let me just be open, the office of the IG belongs to Malawians and you can come to demand information.”

a465.speaker: Meryln Yolamu, Inspector General of the Malawi Police Service
a465.name: Meryln Yolamu
a465.title: Inspector General of the Malawi Police Service
a465.speech: In an earlier response at a conference where these concerns were also raised, Yolamu said: “I know people have lost trust in the Police and it’s not just here, this is the case in many countries, why, because of constant interaction it has with the members of the general public, but I have done my best.”

a583.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a583.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) data
a583.speech: According to data from the OECD, Nigeria has received over $36.16 billion in official development assistance (ODA) between 2015 and 2022.

a583.speaker: Raul Prebisch and Andre Gunder Frank, scholars (Dependency Theory)
a583.name: Raul Prebisch and Andre Gunder Frank
a583.title: scholars (Dependency Theory)
a583.speech: The Dependency Theory, as opined by scholars such as Raul Prebisch and Andre Gunder Frank, states that underdeveloped countries will remain subordinate to developed nations due to their reliance on them for capital, technology, and market access.

a672.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a672.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.speech: "ELF is the only global online Leadership Development Program dedicated to young women aged between 16 and 21. It is designed and delivered by seasoned coaches and leadership practitioners. Each course is three months long and there will be three in a year. The ELF program aims to help young women discover their own expression of leadership and learn to apply it. They will learn competences such as emotional intelligence, conflict management, time management..." ; "All the learning in lectures, coaching and in peer group discussions will be framed by the four pillars of self-responsibility, environmental responsibility, social responsibility and financial responsibility." ; "ELF will provide a space where young women - along with their peers from around the world, will be able to harness their own potential and evolve in accordance with their own vision of their lives." ; "The ELF Program will also support young women to expand their career and professional paths by holding regular talks with various guest speakers..."

a672.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a672.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.speech: On the benefits of the training: "The ELF program is a space where young women will be nurtured and developed; they will be introduced to leadership development, professional coaching and will be exposed to other cultures and individuals from around the world."

a672.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a672.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.speech: On limiting participants to 100: "The first intake in January 2021 is the inaugural cohort; we call those participants Founding Members. They will be pioneers in a brand new program which will certainly grow course by course. Our Founding Members will always be the ones that new participants look to for guidance and inspiration as they embark on the journey."

a672.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a672.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.speech: On the 16-21 age limit: "We want to have young women who are between the age of finishing secondary school and before finishing college. This is a very special age and we feel that if we can equip young women at this age with leadership skills, it will have the most impact... It will be a bit like being taken aside by older, successful women who will tell you what they wished they had been told at that age."

a672.speaker: Yene Assegid (PhD), founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.name: Yene Assegid (PhD)
a672.title: founder of the EveryonesWorld Leadership Foundation program
a672.speech: On reaching girls in sub-Saharan Africa without internet access: "The program is fully online and is available to all young women everywhere. It is a requirement to have Internet access. Part of the reason why we are developing a scholarship system is to assist participants who are unable to pay the tuition fee and may need some help in Internet access. It is our dream to have the funding for at least 50% of the participants and we are encouraging corporates and other donors to become involved by sponsoring groups of participants... We are reaching out to certain companies in different regions with this in mind."

a769.speaker: Abdoulkader Garba, official of the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration of Niger
a769.name: Abdoulkader Garba
a769.title: official of the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration of Niger
a769.speech: In his opening speech, recalled that peace and stability constitute fundamental priorities for Niger. “The prolonged conflicts and insecurity linked to the activity of instrumentalised non-state armed groups have caused deep human suffering and tested the resilience of our society,” he stressed, pointing to the commitment of the country’s highest authorities to offer prospects of reintegration to ex-combatants, ensure appropriate care and promote the reconstruction of a harmonious social fabric ; said the success of this strategy rests on the commitment of all stakeholders: “We have a collective responsibility to ensure that the reintegration of ex-combatants and the care of persons associated with armed groups is carried out with respect for human rights, national security and the needs of local communities” ; according to him, “this challenge is immense but it matches the determination and the aspiration for a peaceful and prosperous Niger within the framework of the great refoundation desired by the people.”

a769.speaker: Abdoulaye Balde, representative of the UNDP
a769.name: Abdoulaye Balde
a769.title: representative of the UNDP
a769.speech: Congratulated the Minister of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration for his leadership in drafting the national DDR/R strategy and for the commitment he had shown in reaching this stage, recalling that the process began in August 2024 with the training of the technical committee members on the principles, methods and approaches of DDR, followed by the drafting and validation of the draft diagnostic report, the regional consultations, and today the synthesis and validation workshop ; “This workshop aims to examine and validate the results of the regional consultations that were carried out by the national technical committee from 27 November to 11 December 2024 in all the regions of Niger,” he stressed, reporting that the regional consultations made it possible to collect data on security threats and to map non-state armed groups in order to refine the analysis and finalise the diagnostic report ; praised the dynamism of the national coordination of stabilisation programmes and of the handling of the surrender of ex-combatants of non-state armed groups, which supports the national technical committee with limited resources.

a769.speaker: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane, Governor of the Dosso region
a769.name: Colonel-Major Bana Alhassane
a769.title: Governor of the Dosso region
a769.speech: Expressed his satisfaction that the region had been chosen to host this meeting, and recalled that the national consultations mission passed through Dosso from 25 to 27 November 2024 and that on that occasion the region made a significant contribution, expressing the hope that the region’s concerns would be taken into account during the proceedings.

a809.speaker: Press note (nota) on the book
a809.name: Press note (nota) on the book
a809.speech: According to the note, the book is an “autofiction” that interweaves the life experiences of Bia Marta with the imaginary world dreamt up by her daughter, Ressurreição Graça.

a809.speaker: Ressurreição Graça, co-author of the book
a809.name: Ressurreição Graça
a809.title: co-author of the book
a809.speech: According to Ressurreição Graça, the work “transports us to a time when women in Cape Verde and, in particular, on the islands of Sal and São Nicolau, unwilling to accept the ungrateful fate that seemed to await them, knew how to reinvent themselves, facing social and cultural challenges with courage and determination, in a silent struggle for dignity and equality.”

a907.speaker: Said Abdullahi Deni, President of Puntland State
a907.name: Said Abdullahi Deni
a907.title: President of Puntland State
a907.speech: Thanked the United States Government for the air support it provided to the operation to clear ISIS militants from the Calmiskaad mountains in Bari region.

a907.speaker: United States (government)
a907.name: United States (government)
a907.speech: Praised the Puntland operation to eradicate the militants and the major successes achieved by the Puntland State forces.

a907.speaker: Somali Broadcasting Corporation (SBC)
a907.name: Somali Broadcasting Corporation (SBC)
a907.speech: “SBC is non Governmental media group (Radio, Television and Internet), SBC was established in June 2001 and its first FM Radio established in Puntland/North Eastern Somalia region.”

a975.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, economic justice and accountability champion for the All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) in Malawi
a975.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
a975.title: economic justice and accountability champion for the All Africa Conference of Churches (AACC) in Malawi
a975.speech: Urged the Malawi government to prioritize transparency and accountability throughout the 2025 General Elections process to prevent suspicions of electoral malpractice. ; Faulted the government for failing to provide regular updates on the NRB’s operations at Kanengo, which he said could have avoided the ensuing controversy. “It is clear that many Malawians were unaware of this arrangement. The lack of communication has created unnecessary suspicion. Ahead of the elections, transparency and regular updates are critical to maintaining public trust.”

a975.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
a975.title: economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.speech: Emphasized that security is a key component of electoral transparency, noting that the absence of law enforcement at the Kanengo facility allowed the MPs to make potentially misleading accusations. “Part of transparency is ensuring that sensitive facilities like the Kanengo warehouse are secure. Without proper security, allegations of electoral malpractice will persist, whether true or not.”

a975.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
a975.title: economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.speech: Called for collaborative efforts by the government, electoral stakeholders, and development partners to regularly inform the public about the progress of voter registration and other electoral processes. “Transparency must be at the core of every stage of the electoral process. The government and its partners should proactively share information to dispel any suspicions. This would prevent situations like the Kanengo incident from escalating.”

a975.speaker: Rev. Baxton Maulidi, economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.name: Rev. Baxton Maulidi
a975.title: economic justice and accountability champion for the AACC in Malawi
a975.speech: Urged whistleblowers to act responsibly, ensuring that allegations are backed by evidence to avoid creating panic or undermining public confidence in the electoral process.

a975.speaker: George Chaponda, Leader of Opposition
a975.name: George Chaponda
a975.title: Leader of Opposition
a975.speech: Accused the government of colluding with the National Registration Bureau (NRB) to compromise voter registration, and alleged the Kanengo facility was being used for suspicious activities after finding thousands of national IDs on the warehouse floor, some packed in sacks.

a975.speaker: National Registration Bureau (NRB)
a975.name: National Registration Bureau (NRB)
a975.speech: Clarified that the facility was part of a 2017 arrangement supported by international development partners, including the UNDP, EU, and USAID, to ensure continuous national registration and efficient distribution of IDs.

a1122.speaker: 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (GDHS)
a1122.name: 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (GDHS)
a1122.speech: Statistics indicate that one in every 10 (10.9%) adolescents aged 15 to 19 years has ever had a live birth. The percentage of adolescents who have had a live birth increases with age, with 19-year-olds recording the highest rate of almost a quarter (23.8%).

a1122.speaker: MSI Reproductive Choices, Ghana (the writer/organisation)
a1122.name: MSI Reproductive Choices
a1122.title: Ghana (the writer/organisation)
a1122.speech: "This moment demands urgent advocacy and decisive diplomacy. We call on: The Government of Ghana and the Ministry of Health to act immediately to safeguard access to contraceptives and champion the reproductive rights of Ghanaian women and girls. The Belgian and French Embassies in Accra should engage their governments and prevent the destruction of these vital supplies. Civil society organisations, women's groups and the media to raise their voices and keep attention on this looming crisis." ; "This is not just a logistical or policy matter, it is a question of life, dignity and justice. Bureaucracy and ideology must not be allowed to burn away the future of Ghanaian women and girls, and millions of women and girls around Africa."

a1122.speaker: Adija, a 17-year-old student, Upper East Region
a1122.name: Adija
a1122.title: a 17-year-old student, Upper East Region
a1122.speech: "Family Planning has helped me stay in school. After giving birth to my son, I can now pursue my dreams of becoming an engineer. Burning them is like stealing that future from me and other girls like me."

a1170.speaker: Nigerian government
a1170.name: Nigerian government
a1170.speech: Has pledged to enhance domestic production of HIV Commodities to meet local needs and support neighbouring West African countries to sustain the HIV response at the 25th International AIDS Conference (AIDS2024).

a1170.speaker: Tunji Alausa, Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.name: Tunji Alausa
a1170.title: Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.speech: Disclosed in Munich, Germany, during the Nigeria Day celebration organised by NACA at the sidelines of the AIDS 2024 conference that Nigeria aims to enhance domestic production to meet the increasing demand for these vital resources within the country while also extending support to neighboring West African nations ; "Thus enhancing the capacity for domestic production of HIV commodities will not only meet local needs but also enable the country to support neighboring West African countries and sustain the HIV response in the country."

a1170.speaker: Tunji Alausa, Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.name: Tunji Alausa
a1170.title: Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.speech: Noted that the removal of Duties on Pharmaceutical Products by President Bola Tinubu is a policy designed to encourage local production and improve health outcomes for Nigerians ; "These government policies are in harmony with the innovative researches and abstracts technical presentations by HIV partners in Nigeria." He urged all stakeholders, both domestic and international, to partner with the government in transforming the country's health system, starting with the HIV programme.

a1170.speaker: Tunji Alausa, Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.name: Tunji Alausa
a1170.title: Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.speech: Assured that no Nigerian will be denied access to services for HIV based on their sexual orientation, saying the government recognises the importance of a public health approach in addressing legal and policy concerns, particularly regarding key populations in Nigeria: "As I emphasised during my meeting with the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS), no one will be denied services based on their sexual orientation. However, while we uphold our laws, we are committed to ensuring that everyone - key populations including those in custodial centres, receive the necessary health services."

a1170.speaker: Tunji Alausa, Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.name: Tunji Alausa
a1170.title: Nigerian Minister of State for Health
a1170.speech: Said the theme of AIDS 2024, 'Putting People First,' aligns perfectly with the renewed hope agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, adding that the theme resonates deeply with the administration's Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp) for the health sector in Nigeria, which is centered on innovative and sustainable solutions.

a1170.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a1170.name: Temitope Ilori
a1170.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a1170.speech: Said ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030 is a goal that can only be achieved through our collective efforts. She said the country's HIV programme has been significantly dependent on donor funding. She further said, "As we strive towards epidemic control, we must confront some challenging questions: What happens when partners withdraw their financial support for HIV? Can we develop a robust system that provides health insurance for people living with HIV and other vulnerable populations in the country?"

a1183.speaker: G7 foreign ministers of Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States, together with the European Union's foreign policy chief (statement)
a1183.name: G7 foreign ministers of Canada
a1183.title: France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States, together with the European Union's foreign policy chief (statement)
a1183.speech: Condemned the ongoing M23 offensive in eastern DRC and urged "the M23 and the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) to cease their offensive in all directions," calling for the "urgent protection of civilians"; also called for an end to "all direct or indirect support" to the M23 and to all non-state armed groups in Congo. "This offensive constitutes a flagrant disregard for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC. We also condemn the M23's intention to continue its expansion into South Kivu." ; Said the latest M23 offensive has caused a dramatic increase in displaced civilians in Goma and across eastern DRC: "We deplore the devastating consequences of the new M23 and RDF offensive, which are worsening already difficult humanitarian conditions." ; Called for "rapid, safe and unhindered" passage of humanitarian aid for civilians and reiterated that humanitarian personnel must be given security guarantees; called on all parties to return to the negotiating table and to "honour their commitments under the Luanda process," and urged the M23 to withdraw from all areas under its control; reiterated the G7's full support for MONUSCO to protect civilians and stabilise the region, calling on all parties to respect its mandate.

a1183.speaker: M23 (March 23 Movement)
a1183.name: M23 (March 23 Movement)
a1183.speech: Claimed to have seized the city of Goma after launching a major offensive last week.

a1183.speaker: Rwanda / Kigali
a1183.name: Rwanda / Kigali
a1183.speech: Denies supporting the group; rejects the allegations, asserting that the M23 is a Congolese movement led by Congolese, even though its members speak Kinyarwanda; also rejects the conclusions of the UN reports and recalls having disarmed the M23 rebels who had taken refuge on its soil in 2012-2013 before handing their arsenal over to the Congolese authorities.

a1183.speaker: Kinshasa (Government of the DRC)
a1183.name: Kinshasa (Government of the DRC)
a1183.speech: Accuses Rwanda of actively supporting the M23 in order to gain access to the region's mineral wealth; for the DRC, the M23 is a "terrorist" group and any form of negotiation is categorically rejected.

a1183.speaker: Reports by UN agencies
a1183.name: Reports by UN agencies
a1183.speech: Support the accusations, pointing to Rwandan military backing for the rebel movement.

a1183.speaker: Kigali (Government of Rwanda)
a1183.name: Kigali (Government of Rwanda)
a1183.speech: Says the M23 represents a threat to its internal security and accuses the DRC of collaborating with armed groups, notably the Wazalendo militias and the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), considered responsible for the Rwandan genocide; according to Kigali these alliances are part of a strategy aimed at overthrowing the Rwandan government.

a1218.speaker: Yokohama Declaration (TICAD9 communique)
a1218.name: Yokohama Declaration (TICAD9 communique)
a1218.speech: Reaffirmed support for multilateral trade and outlined plans to deepen ties between Africa and the Indo-Pacific region, aligning with Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba's new economic initiative; the declaration emphasized industrial cooperation, human resource development and private-sector investment.

a1218.speaker: Ronald Porusingazi, political analyst
a1218.name: Ronald Porusingazi
a1218.title: political analyst
a1218.speech: "The optics of 34 one-on-one meetings suggest a divide-and-engage strategy rather than a collective African front." ; "It's hard to see how this format strengthens the African Continental Free Trade Area or supports Agenda 2063's vision of a unified, prosperous continent." ; expressed concern that this could sideline regional institutions and continental frameworks.

a1218.speaker: Shigeru Ishiba, Japanese Prime Minister
a1218.name: Shigeru Ishiba
a1218.title: Japanese Prime Minister
a1218.speech: Stressed the importance of understanding each country's unique needs.

a1218.speaker: Ronald Porusingazi, political analyst
a1218.name: Ronald Porusingazi
a1218.title: political analyst
a1218.speech: "While Japan announced a $5.5 billion collaborative framework with the African Development Bank to support youth, women and regional connectivity, the lack of a unified African negotiating bloc at TICAD9 may limit the continent's leverage in shaping such initiatives." ; noted that as global powers compete for influence in Africa, the continent's leaders face a strategic choice – whether to engage individually for short-term gains or collectively to advance long-term integration ; "TICAD9 offered both opportunities and contradictions. Whether it strengthens Africa's continental agenda or scatters it across bilateral tracks will depend on what happens next."

a1672.speaker: Ministry of Health of Djibouti (source of the report)
a1672.name: Ministry of Health of Djibouti (source of the report)
a1672.speech: Stated that these acceleration activities once again reflect the Ministry of Health's determination to improve the accessibility and quality of care provision at all levels of the health pyramid, with particular emphasis on maternal and child health, and that it is with this in mind that the ministry decided to strengthen the existing arrangements for the routine vaccination of children under five and for Covid-19 vaccination through the implementation of a vast plan to deploy mobile teams and multiply immunisation sites, in order to rapidly achieve optimal vaccination coverage. The health department will make new means of transport available to field teams, including 5 vaccination TUK TUKs and 4 4x4 vehicles, in order to bring vaccination closer to families furthest from health facilities. The implementation of these vaccination intensification activities follows a recent enumeration survey carried out by the Ministry of Health on the vaccination rate of children under five, screening for malnourished children and antenatal consultations for pregnant women.

a1717.speaker: African Union Commission (AUC) (announcement)
a1717.name: African Union Commission (AUC) (announcement)
a1717.speech: Announced that the AUC, in collaboration with the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia's Ministry of Labour and Skills, will host the second edition of Africa Skills Week from 13-17 October 2025 at the African Union Headquarters in Addis Ababa, under the theme "Powering Africa's Industrial Future: Skills for Innovation, Growth, and Sustainability," and that the event is expected to accelerate implementation of the Continental TVET Strategy 2025-2034, strengthen alignment between skills development and Africa's industrialization strategies, showcase innovative models linking training with employment and entrepreneurship, and elevate youth, women, and entrepreneurs as key drivers of Africa's industrial transformation.

a1717.speaker: H.E. Ali Youssouf Mohammed, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a1717.name: H.E. Ali Youssouf Mohammed
a1717.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a1717.speech: Emphasized: "Africa Skills Week 2025 represents our collective resolve to transform Africa's demographic dividend into a dynamic workforce that powers industrial growth, sustainability, and innovation across the continent."

a1717.speaker: H.E. Muferihat Kamil Ahmed, Minister of Labour and Skills of Ethiopia
a1717.name: H.E. Muferihat Kamil Ahmed
a1717.title: Minister of Labour and Skills of Ethiopia
a1717.speech: Noted: "Hosting this continental platform in Addis Ababa reflects Ethiopia's commitment to inclusive skills development, including opportunities for refugees and displaced populations, as part of our shared African industrial future."

a1755.speaker: Government of Mozambique and the United States Embassy (joint announcement)
a1755.name: Government of Mozambique and the United States Embassy (joint announcement)
a1755.speech: Announced, this Monday in Maputo, the $537 million financing agreement under the second Compact of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), stating that the money comes from the United States of America and will be used for the construction of climate-resilient infrastructure, coastal development and the strengthening of local economies in Zambézia province that depend on agriculture and fisheries.

a1868.speaker: Gladys Ganda, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.name: Gladys Ganda
a1868.title: Chairperson of the Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.speech: Has said the 3.2% economic projections done by the Minister of Finance Simplex Chithyola Banda in his Budget Statement is like 'whitewashed tomb because inside the budget it is full of dead bones and everything found is unclean.' She was speaking in Parliament on Monday, March 17, 2025 responding to the Budget Statement issued by Minister of Finance Simplex Chithyola Banda on February 28, 2025 and the strategic actions required for fiscal sustainability.

a1868.speaker: Gladys Ganda, Chairperson of the Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.name: Gladys Ganda
a1868.title: Chairperson of the Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.speech: Condemned government for poor economic policies which are putting the country under constant inflationary pressure caused by persistent borrowing and overspending, triggering inflation at 32.3% as the budget deficit is now forecasted at MK2.473 trillion while the national debt stands at MK16.19 trillion, a huge burden to poor Malawians: "Madam Speaker, the current state of our economy, though unfortunate, is not shocking. The Committee has repeatedly highlighted persistent economic challenges, yet these issues continue to undermine our fiscal stability. There is growing concern over whether the proposed fiscal policy measures will sufficiently address the root causes of our financial distress, particularly the unsustainable levels of debt that continue to burden our nation. The failure to curb our borrowing appetite, even as government expenditures rise, is a matter of serious concern." ; "Madam Speaker, on our greatest weaknesses has been our failure to address urgent matters with the necessary sense of urgency. Allocating resources to well-structured projects with clear timelines, particularly those that directly combat hunger and reduce import dependency in the short term, would have been a more strategic approach while working towards long-term solutions. Unfortunately, as a nation, we have struggled with a lack of focus and frequently misplaced priorities. Madam Speaker, our resource envelope is already small, yet we continue to spread ourselves too thinly across too many initiatives without tangible results. It is imperative that we take a more disciplined and strategic approach to resource allocation, focusing on initiatives that yield meaningful outcomes for our people. It is only through such decisive action that we can place our economy on a sustainable path and secure a better future for our nation."

a1868.speaker: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.name: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.speech: According to Ganda, the Committee is also concerned about the recent volatility in foreign financing, with some donors such as USAID having withdrawn funding.

a1868.speaker: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.name: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.speech: Has welcomed the government position on a number of tax measures such as Income Tax and VAT on basic needs such as bread and confectioneries, as such a move will ease financial burdens on households; said removal of tax on irrigation equipment through Customs and Excise Tax is a very important intervention to improve agricultural productivity amid climate-related challenges, and that elimination of excise tax on hybrid vehicles will promote eco-friendly transport among other measures.

a1868.speaker: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.name: Parliamentary Budget and Finance Committee of Malawi
a1868.speech: Has recommended several measures as one way of bringing back the economy to life, asking government to enhance revenue mobilisation, strengthen debt management and reduce borrowing, improve budget transparency and accuracy, strengthen agricultural resilience, address the high cost of inputs, and enhance budget flexibility and fiscal space among others.

a1905.speaker: Centre for Investigative Journalism Malawi
a1905.name: Centre for Investigative Journalism Malawi
a1905.speech: "Families forage for wild yams; hospitals turn away patients; youth sell bananas at intersections. Chakwera's 'New Malawi' is a graveyard of hope."

a1905.speaker: Transparency International
a1905.name: Transparency International
a1905.speech: Ranked Malawi 107/180 nations (CPI score: 34/100); "systemic rot" cited.

a1905.speaker: UK National Crime Agency (NCA)
a1905.name: UK National Crime Agency (NCA)
a1905.speech: Implicated 80+ officials in the Sattar bribes; local prosecutions stalled.

a1971.speaker: Save the Children International (SCI) Nigeria
a1971.name: Save the Children International (SCI) Nigeria
a1971.speech: Says that over 150,000 children have been displaced by flooding in Borno State and are in dire need of humanitarian assistance.

a1971.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.name: Duncan Harvey
a1971.title: Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.speech: Made the disclosure on Wednesday in Abuja while briefing newsmen about his visit to Maiduguri; said that over 300,000 people had been registered in at least 26 relocation sites as of September 14, adding that up to 30 sites had been set up, while registration was ongoing; said more than 400,000 persons were affected by the floods in the state with 37 deaths and 58 people injured ; “So we can estimate that around 150,000 of the people living in those camps are children, and therefore that’s a very real cause of concern. We need to protect those children, provide them with health and nutrition, make sure they have access to clean water, and also ensure that they have appropriate care in place.”

a1971.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.name: Duncan Harvey
a1971.title: Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.speech: Said Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camps were overcrowded and unsanitary, noting that the scale of partners' services was not keeping up with the numbers; said that the flooding happened at the height of a food and nutrition crisis, lamenting that “in addition to the immediate need for food and clean water for IDPs, water-borne diseases and malaria are major risks. Open defecation in the camps is widespread.”

a1971.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.name: Duncan Harvey
a1971.title: Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.speech: Called on Borno State and the Federal Governments to ensure that humanitarian actors are supported and encouraged with enabling approaches and systems that help speed up response programme for children, families and communities in urgent need.

a1971.speaker: Duncan Harvey, Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.name: Duncan Harvey
a1971.title: Country Director of Save the Children International (SCI)
a1971.speech: Said SCI was providing urgent rescue service, life-saving response and rehabilitation for the affected communities in the state, and was also working in collaboration with the state government and other humanitarian actors: “SCI’s urgent response plan to the crises includes but not limited to Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to the affected households, setting up health and nutrition outreach services to the affected households, rehabilitation of sanitation facilities, and conducting hygiene promotion and community awareness, child protection in emergencies through setting up mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) help desk to provide psychological first aid and psychological support to children and caregivers in the camp among others.”

a1985.speaker: Food Crop Contractors Association (FCCA)
a1985.name: Food Crop Contractors Association (FCCA)
a1985.speech: Has warned that the proposed ban on the importation of cereals by the government could result in abrupt shortages and disruption to processors' supply chains.

a1985.speaker: Anxious Masuka, Zimbabwean Agriculture minister (Crops, Livestock and Fisheries Assessment 2024/25 summer season report)
a1985.name: Anxious Masuka
a1985.title: Zimbabwean Agriculture minister (Crops, Livestock and Fisheries Assessment 2024/25 summer season report)
a1985.speech: Made recommendations in the report which suggest that cereal imports should be [banned/restricted].

a2187.speaker: US Agency for International Development (USAID) document
a2187.name: US Agency for International Development (USAID) document
a2187.speech: Revealed that the Donald Trump administration is planning to scale back its malaria interventions; states that a total of 5,341 awards will be cancelled, amounting to nearly $76 billion, of which the government has already committed to spending about $48 billion, and that the US will be terminating the majority of its health projects and interventions, including those related to malaria.

a2187.speaker: Reuters
a2187.name: Reuters
a2187.speech: Reported that the document, outlining a list of international aid programmes set to be dismantled and those that will be retained, was shared with US lawmakers on Wednesday.

a2187.speaker: US State Department spokesperson
a2187.name: US State Department spokesperson
a2187.speech: Said the projects that were terminated were those that failed to meet those priorities or advance US national interest: "Each award terminated was reviewed individually for alignment with agency and administration priorities. Critical USAID programme awards remain active."

a2187.speaker: Sania Nishtar, GAVI chief executive officer
a2187.name: Sania Nishtar
a2187.title: GAVI chief executive officer
a2187.speech: Insists that millions of children will die as a result of the US cutbacks; told Reuters that the US annual $300 million funding is vital for its operation ; "If we don't get US support, that translates into 1.2 million deaths over the next five years, among children who will be unprotected against deadly diseases like measles and diphtheria" ; "I really look forward to engaging. We hope that a final decision has not been made."

a2187.speaker: Premium Times (earlier report)
a2187.name: Premium Times (earlier report)
a2187.speech: Reported the termination of 83 percent of USAID programmes and 5,200 contracts awarded by the agency.

a2264.speaker: Lydia Yaako Donkor, Director-General of the CID, Commissioner of Police (COP)
a2264.name: Lydia Yaako Donkor
a2264.title: Director-General of the CID, Commissioner of Police (COP)
a2264.speech: Speaking at a joint press conference with the Cyber Security Authority (CSA) in Accra, disclosed that the main suspect in the murder of Assistant Inspector of Immigration Stephen King Amoah had been arrested and charged with murder ; "He is currently on remand following his appearance before the Adabraka District Court and is scheduled to reappear on August 8, 2025. A special operation is currently underway to identify and arrest his accomplices, and we are following other vital leads to gather all necessary evidence against the suspect and his accomplices" ; Assured the public that the investigation remained ongoing and that every effort was being made to ensure all the perpetrators were brought to justice.

a2264.speaker: Criminal Investigations Department (CID), Ghana Police Service
a2264.name: Criminal Investigations Department (CID)
a2264.title: Ghana Police Service
a2264.speech: Announced the arrest of Abubakari Sadick, a fugitive convicted in absentia for a 2021 robbery and linked to multiple car robbery cases across the country.

a2264.speaker: Police investigation records
a2264.name: Police investigation records
a2264.speech: Investigations revealed that Mr Amoah had left home the previous evening to meet a man identified as Bright Aweh, who had sent him WhatsApp images of cash and asked to settle an outstanding debt; the suspect, who initially admitted to handing over GH¢500,000 to the deceased, was arrested and charged with kidnapping, but following the discovery of Mr Amoah's burnt body and forensic evidence, including bloodstains, burnt fabrics, and a bloodied fufu pestle, the charge was upgraded to murder.

a2264.speaker: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor, Director-General of the CID
a2264.name: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor
a2264.title: Director-General of the CID
a2264.speech: Stated that Mr Sadick and his accomplices often posed as NGO workers to rent vehicles for supposed missionary work before attacking drivers and stealing the vehicles ; Added that the syndicate operated mainly in the northern region, that he was placed on multiple watchlists, including an INTERPOL Red Notice, and was finally arrested in Accra on July 28, 2025.

a2264.speaker: Ghana Police Service / COP Lydia Yaako Donkor, Director-General of the CID
a2264.name: Ghana Police Service / COP Lydia Yaako Donkor
a2264.title: Director-General of the CID
a2264.speech: Reported progress in a January 1 robbery involving a taxi driver, Vic Martin Obeng, who was attacked at Haatso by three passengers posing as commuters ; Revealed that the suspects robbed him of his sales, mobile phone, and GH¢13,000 in mobile money ; Stated that, acting on intelligence, police arrested one suspect, Vincent Gbetorglo, an ex-convict previously sentenced to 40 years in prison, who was found in possession of the victim's stolen phone.

a2264.speaker: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor, Director-General of the CID
a2264.name: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor
a2264.title: Director-General of the CID
a2264.speech: Said that of 43 high-end vehicles stolen from countries including the USA, Canada and several EU nations and impounded with INTERPOL Ghana and other international partners, 18 had been repatriated by the courts, while the rest were under legal review ; Added that a special task force had also seized six additional vehicles linked to money laundering and cyber-enabled crimes such as romance fraud and sextortion.

a2264.speaker: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor, Director-General of the CID
a2264.name: COP Lydia Yaako Donkor
a2264.title: Director-General of the CID
a2264.speech: Urged the public to exercise due diligence when purchasing imported vehicles, adding, "Let me indicate here that payment of customs duties in Ghana does not mean that the vehicle was legitimately acquired from the country of origin" ; Reaffirmed the CID's commitment to due process, transparency, and justice, calling on the public to support ongoing investigations by volunteering credible information.

a2417.speaker: Various data sources including IMF, Statista, World Bank and Bloomberg (2021-2024 average figures)
a2417.name: Various data sources including IMF
a2417.title: Statista, World Bank and Bloomberg (2021-2024 average figures)
a2417.speech: Cited as the source of GDP comparison figures: California (USA) GDP $4.0 trillion, larger than the combined GDP of Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt and Kenya; Texas $2.4 trillion; New York State $2.2 trillion; Germany $4.5 trillion; the Netherlands $1.0 trillion; and Africa's largest economies - Nigeria $477 billion, South Africa $399 billion, Egypt $474 billion, Kenya $110 billion, Ghana $82 billion.

a2523.speaker: Jean Ping, African Union chairman
a2523.name: Jean Ping
a2523.title: African Union chairman
a2523.speech: “This is what we pledged today, it is new money and exclusively African.”

a2833.speaker: Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2021 Ethiopia policy brief by Alliance 2015 (report)
a2833.name: Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2021 Ethiopia policy brief by Alliance 2015 (report)
a2833.speech: It painted a bleak picture, reporting that humanitarian assistance needs have increased by 40pc compared to last year. It also showed that "progress in the fight against chronic food insecurity and malnutrition is decelerating."

a2916.speaker: Antonia Piri Piri, AMAMUS Coordinator and advocate for disability-inclusive health services
a2916.name: Antonia Piri Piri
a2916.title: AMAMUS Coordinator and advocate for disability-inclusive health services
a2916.speech: Said her organisation was ready to reach out to beneficiaries who depend on them “not only for healthcare but also for reassurance, understanding and a sense of connection.”

a2954.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.name: Bill Gates
a2954.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.speech: Issued a stark but hopeful call to world leaders to save millions of children's lives and make some of the deadliest diseases history by 2045: “Humanity is at a crossroads. With millions of children’s lives on the line, global leaders have a once-in-a-generation chance to do something extraordinary. The choices they make now—whether to go forward with proposed steep cuts to health aid or to give the world’s children the chance they deserve to live a healthy life—will determine what kind of future we leave the next generation.” ; “What’s happening to the health of the world’s children is worse than most people realize, but our long-term prospects are better than most people can imagine. I don’t expect most governments to suddenly restore foreign aid to historic levels, but I am an optimist, and I believe governments can and will do what’s needed to save as many children as possible.”

a2954.speaker: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) (recent study)
a2954.name: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) (recent study)
a2954.speech: According to a recent study by the IHME, global development assistance for health fell by 21% between 2024 and 2025, and is now at a 15-year low.

a2954.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.name: Bill Gates
a2954.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.speech: Announced his foundation's pledge of $912 million over three years to the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria's 2026-2028 replenishment.

a2954.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.name: Bill Gates
a2954.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.speech: “We have a roadmap for saving millions of children and making some of the deadliest childhood diseases history by 2045. I’m urging world leaders to invest in the health of all people, especially children, to deliver this future.”

a2954.speaker: Gates Foundation and IHME (research results)
a2954.name: Gates Foundation and IHME (research results)
a2954.speech: Results indicate that sustaining global investments in child health and scaling lifesaving innovations could cut child deaths in half again over the next 20 years.

a2954.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.name: Bill Gates
a2954.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a2954.speech: “An entire generation is alive today thanks to the world’s generosity, smart investments, and the hard work of governments and Global Fund partners. Now, we must go further so the next generation grows up in a world where no child dies from preventable causes.”

a2954.speaker: Gates Foundation
a2954.name: Gates Foundation
a2954.speech: Announced President of the Government of Spain Pedro Sánchez as the winner of its 2025 Global Goalkeeper Award, in recognition of his continued commitment to advance the Global Goals.

a2954.speaker: Jon Batiste, singer, songwriter and composer, and Olivia Wilde, actress and director (event co-hosts)
a2954.name: Jon Batiste
a2954.title: singer, songwriter and composer, and Olivia Wilde, actress and director (event co-hosts)
a2954.speech: Urged the audience to remember that while the world has made progress, “we can’t stop at almost.”

a2954.speaker: Dawda Jobarteh, deputy director of the Gates Foundation's Goalkeepers campaign
a2954.name: Dawda Jobarteh
a2954.title: deputy director of the Gates Foundation's Goalkeepers campaign
a2954.speech: “Every year, Goalkeepers unites changemakers to inspire and push one another forward. Together, we can reimagine a future without preventable child deaths and unlock the next wave of breakthroughs for the world’s children.”

a2968.speaker: Director General of PDSA / DMP (Djibouti Multipurpose Port)
a2968.name: Director General of PDSA / DMP (Djibouti Multipurpose Port)
a2968.speech: Gave a presentation of the Djibouti ports “as a regional and international platform” in order to demonstrate that DMP is a key factor in the delivery of USAID food aid products destined for the region, and to affirm the primary role that Djibouti plays in improving the logistics chain across the Horn of Africa thanks to its geostrategic position as the Hinterland's Hub.

a2968.speaker: PDSA / DMP (Djibouti Multipurpose Port) (statement)
a2968.name: PDSA / DMP (Djibouti Multipurpose Port) (statement)
a2968.speech: Stated that DMP is practically ready in terms of infrastructure, equipment, qualified labour and terminal operating systems; that all standards for combating cargo infestation risks are already implemented at DMP with best practices and permanent PEST Control monitoring in order to reduce the incidence of food-borne diseases and ensure a safe supply for people in need; and that the first USAID food aid vessel, MV Silver Lady, docked at DMP on 13/10/2024 with a tonnage of 30,970 MT of sorghum, with DMP remaining firm in its commitment to unloading performance within a short time frame.

a3226.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3226.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3226.title: President of Ghana
a3226.speech: Reiterated his administration's dedication to fiscal policies that prioritised citizens' welfare: "Promises made, promises delivered," he said after appending his signature to the repealed Bills ; added that "these taxes were not only burdensome but also hindered economic activity. Their removal will empower businesses, encourage digital transactions, and promote sustainable development."

a3226.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister of Ghana
a3226.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a3226.title: Finance Minister of Ghana
a3226.speech: Said in a brief statement after the President assented to the bill that the Electronic Transfer Levy (Repeal) Bill was part of the government's tax reform agenda to improve the disposable incomes of households and reduce the overall tax burden of taxpayers; said the removal of the E-Levy would not only result in increased disposable income for Ghanaian households and individuals, it would also provide financial relief to companies that patronise the E-Levy: "This policy aligns with the government's broader commitment to fostering economic growth and enhancing financial inclusion" ; added that the repeal of the E-Levy would encourage the government's objective of achieving a cash-lite economy, saying it was also expected to stimulate digital transactions, encourage financial innovation, and ease the cost of doing business.

a3226.speaker: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister of Ghana
a3226.name: Dr Cassiel Ato Forson
a3226.title: Finance Minister of Ghana
a3226.speech: On the VAT (Amendment) Bill, said it amended the Value Added Tax Act, 2013 (Act 870) to exempt the supply of motor vehicle insurance from VAT: "The passage of this Bill will provide relief to households and commuters while ensuring a fair and balanced tax system" ; explained that the repeal of the Emission Levy would enable the government to re-engage stakeholders on environmental reforms that would comprehensively address carbon dioxide emissions from specified sectors and promote the use of eco-friendly technology and green energy: "These reforms also seek to improve environmental management while controlling general levels of air and water pollution locally."

a3226.speaker: Stephen Blewett, Chief Executive Officer of MTN Ghana
a3226.name: Stephen Blewett
a3226.title: Chief Executive Officer of MTN Ghana
a3226.speech: Said although the E-Levy law had been scrapped, the companies that applied the tax must be directed by the regulators to effect them; for that reason, the repeal could not have an immediate impact due to the effect of transmitting instructions, Mr Blewett said in Accra during an interaction with stakeholders as part of his one-year as CEO at MTN Ghana.

a3226.speaker: Dr Ken Ashigbey, Chief Executive of the Ghana Chamber of Telecommunications
a3226.name: Dr Ken Ashigbey
a3226.title: Chief Executive of the Ghana Chamber of Telecommunications
a3226.speech: Said telecommunications service providers who provided electronic transfer services would begin to effect the zero E-Levy charges upon the receipt of notification from the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA); said the assented document from the Presidency was expected to be gazetted and then transmitted to the GRA for implementation; said the GRA would in turn inform the relevant agencies and service providers when to begin to effect the changes, explaining that the various service providers would begin to calibrate their systems to reflect the abolition.

a3226.speaker: National Democratic Congress (NDC)
a3226.name: National Democratic Congress (NDC)
a3226.speech: During its 2024 election campaign, pledged to scrap the levies to foster a more business-friendly environment and ease the cost of living.

a3226.speaker: Critics of the taxes
a3226.name: Critics of the taxes
a3226.speech: Critics argued that the betting tax, E-Levy and emission tax placed undue strain on businesses and individuals without necessarily impacting on the government's revenue mobilisation efforts.

a3388.speaker: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres (report, "Shifting Paradigms: United to Deliver")
a3388.name: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres (report
a3388.title: "Shifting Paradigms: United to Deliver")
a3388.speech: A report which outlines plans to phase out the UN Joint Programme on HIV and Aids (UNAids) by the end of 2026 and proposes integrating UNAids' capacity and expertise into other UN development entities by 2027; among the recommendations is also a potential merger of the UN Development Programme (UNDP) with the UN Office for Project Services and another between the UN Population Fund and UN Women. Guterres says the changes are part of broader reform efforts aimed at improving efficiency and coherence across the UN system.

a3388.speaker: United Nations
a3388.name: United Nations
a3388.speech: The objective, the UN says, is to streamline operations, enhance delivery and reduce overhead costs.

a3388.speaker: UNAids
a3388.name: UNAids
a3388.speech: Has confirmed it is already undergoing a transition in line with the reform agenda and that a two-phase transformation plan, approved by the UNAids Board in June 2025, is currently being implemented; the agency says the second phase, set to begin in 2027, will further consolidate and integrate UNAids' operations with other UN entities and regional institutions such as the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, eventually resulting in the closure of the UNAids Secretariat in its current form.

a3388.speaker: NGO Delegation to the UNAids Programme Coordinating Board
a3388.name: NGO Delegation to the UNAids Programme Coordinating Board
a3388.speech: Has strongly opposed the proposed sunset of UNAids, calling it a betrayal of the global commitment to end Aids by 2030; the group says preserving UNAids is about saving lives and that to propose sunsetting it now is "profoundly dangerous"; it further warns that dismantling UNAids would undermine commitments to people living with HIV and derail progress on the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 3 on health and Goal 10 on reducing inequalities; the group insists that UNAids must remain active until new infections are halted, lifesaving treatment reaches everyone who needs it and the human rights of people living with and affected by HIV are fully protected, and argues any restructuring must strengthen rather than weaken the HIV response and community leadership.

a3388.speaker: International Aids Society (IAS)
a3388.name: International Aids Society (IAS)
a3388.speech: Has urged the UN to keep HIV a priority on the global health agenda; IAS says while it remains committed to working with communities, governments and UN agencies, without clear funding commitments from major donors such as Pepfar and the Global Fund, millions risk losing access to treatment and prevention.

a3388.speaker: David Kamkwamba, Executive Director of the Network of Journalists Living with HIV (Joneha)
a3388.name: David Kamkwamba
a3388.title: Executive Director of the Network of Journalists Living with HIV (Joneha)
a3388.speech: In a written response, highlighted "the critical role UNAids plays in supporting organisations that work with marginalised populations"; warned that in countries like Malawi, where legal and structural barriers still exist, UNAids is essential for setting priorities, tracking progress and holding governments accountable ; "Taking away UNAids risks undoing years of progress in the fight against HIV and Aids," he warned.

a3388.speaker: UNAids
a3388.name: UNAids
a3388.speech: Has warned that recent cuts in global HIV funding could reverse this progress and that without renewed investment, an additional 4.2 million people are expected to die from Aids-related illnesses in the next four years, with an estimated 6.6 million people projected to newly acquire HIV over the same period.

a3489.speaker: United Nations
a3489.name: United Nations
a3489.speech: The United Nations estimates that more people will live in towns and cities than in rural areas by 2026.

a3489.speaker: Refugees International (report)
a3489.name: Refugees International (report)
a3489.speech: According to a report by the US-based rights group Refugees International, most of the millions of people fleeing from rural to urban areas in Somalia are not going home, not now and not ever.

a3489.speaker: Refugees International (report)
a3489.name: Refugees International (report)
a3489.speech: Says "Many long-standing IDPs more closely resemble urban poor and have a different set of needs than new arrivals."

a3489.speaker: Fatima Mohamed Iise, 31, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Fatima Mohamed Iise
a3489.title: 31, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: "We had a very good life as pastoralists. We had about 40 cows. Now we have none so I had no choice but to come to Mogadishu with my children." ; "My nine-year-old daughter and I go out early every morning to look for work. The only jobs we can find are laundry work and tidying up construction sites which pay between $1 and $1.50 a day. This is not enough to pay for basic necessities but it's better than nothing at all." ; "We only have countryside skills and nobody needs these in the city." ; "I use my earnings to buy rice, beans or maize meal. We eat once a day at lunchtime. The rest of the time we drink tea. My children and I go to sleep on empty stomachs."

a3489.speaker: Fatima Mohamed Iise, 31, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Fatima Mohamed Iise
a3489.title: 31, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: On harassment: "Men come to me offering to help me find a job or get some food. Then they say they want something in return. They either want sex or to marry my daughters."

a3489.speaker: Hawa (name changed), 70, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Hawa (name changed)
a3489.title: 70, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: "No sex, no food. The circumstances of my life now are beyond anyone's imagination. It is hard to believe the reason why I no longer receive food aid but that is the truth." ; "The camp manager asked me to engage in some misbehaviour if I wanted food. I asked what he meant and he said he wanted sex. I was shocked and angrily I rejected him. Since then I haven't received a single grain of food." ; says demands for sexual favours are becoming increasingly common in Mogadishu's IDP camps: "Some girls and women agree to have sex with these men. It is so sad."

a3489.speaker: Hawa (name changed), 70, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Hawa (name changed)
a3489.title: 70, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: On harassment at work: "The male shopkeepers and their staff offer women food and extra money in return for sexual favours. The situation is better for IDPs who work in people's houses because it's women who stay at home while men go out to work." ; "The employers who are kindest to us are older women. They sometimes give us extra money."

a3489.speaker: S'iido Hassan Moalim, 66, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: S'iido Hassan Moalim
a3489.title: 66, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: "I live here alone. I believe I am the poorest person in this camp. I cannot see, I cannot work and I have received no voucher cards for food aid." ; "The weak have no rights."

a3489.speaker: S'iido Hassan Moalim, 66, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: S'iido Hassan Moalim
a3489.title: 66, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: On exploitation in the camp: "The residents of this camp who benefit are those who accept the demands of the men in charge. I cannot do that because I am old and I respect my culture which forbids such activities." ; "Nobody respects young girls and women. The men call on them anytime they want. When their needs are satisfied they give them money or food."

a3489.speaker: Iisho Mukhtar Adam, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Iisho Mukhtar Adam
a3489.title: displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: "I wash the clothes and clean the houses of people who are better off than me. I earn between $1 and $2 a day. I work long hours in order to manage the life of my family as best I can." ; explains how IDPs who work in people's houses are occasionally beaten by their employers who sometimes accuse them of stealing their property: "At the end of the day, some people say they don't have money to pay us and that we should come back to following day to collect it. Others don't pay us at all. They have no respect for us. Most employers look down on us but some more educated people treat us as humans."

a3489.speaker: Iisho Mukhtar Adam, displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.name: Iisho Mukhtar Adam
a3489.title: displaced woman in Asal IDP camp
a3489.speech: Says there is nobody to call on for help, as the police tend to be busy dealing with Mogadishu's endless security threats and many are corrupt: "Nobody listens to us. The only thing to do is tell the media about our plight and hope that somebody with the power and resources to do so will help us." ; on sexual abuse in the camp: "I have not yet been asked for sexual favours. Most people keep silent about it because they know that if they complain they will be expelled from the camp."

a3489.speaker: Rahma Mohamed, displaced woman in Allah-dhowr IDP camp
a3489.name: Rahma Mohamed
a3489.title: displaced woman in Allah-dhowr IDP camp
a3489.speech: "Often the people I work for pay me less than what we agreed on. We might agree on $5 but at the end of the day they only pay me $3."

a3489.speaker: Rahma Mohamed, displaced woman in Allah-dhowr IDP camp
a3489.name: Rahma Mohamed
a3489.title: displaced woman in Allah-dhowr IDP camp
a3489.speech: "Despite being viewed as a refugee by the people of Mogadishu, I want to establish my own small business here to support my family."

a3489.speaker: Asmo Abdi Farah Ahmed, 15, displaced girl working as a maid
a3489.name: Asmo Abdi Farah Ahmed
a3489.title: 15, displaced girl working as a maid
a3489.speech: "The children in neighbourhoods surrounding our camp go to school and play together. Sometimes they make fun of me for not going to school. They say I am just a 'village kid'."

a3489.speaker: Sayid Omar, Mogadishu resident
a3489.name: Sayid Omar
a3489.title: Mogadishu resident
a3489.speech: "Although some have lived in the city for years, I hesitate to consider them as full residents. I see them as second-class citizens, even if they settle permanently and integrate into city life. It's true that people in the capital come from different backgrounds but this doesn't automatically grant them equal status or opportunities within the city."

a3489.speaker: Mukhtar Abdalla Abdow, 60, displaced man living in Mogadishu
a3489.name: Mukhtar Abdalla Abdow
a3489.title: 60, displaced man living in Mogadishu
a3489.speech: "People here still consider me a displaced person, a refugee, even though I have lived here for 16 years." ; "I consider myself a local resident."

a3489.speaker: Juweeriya Mohamed Ibrahim, Mogadishu resident
a3489.name: Juweeriya Mohamed Ibrahim
a3489.title: Mogadishu resident
a3489.speech: "I see them as normal people who came here because their lives were threatened by floods, drought and conflict. For me, if they have lived in Mogadishu for more than five years, I consider them to be residents just like me." ; "Others often say they are second-class citizens. I firmly believe they are not."

a3689.speaker: Aïssa Laouan Wandarama, Nigerien Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management
a3689.name: Aïssa Laouan Wandarama
a3689.title: Nigerien Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management
a3689.speech: Announced that her ministerial department is drawing up a strategy for the localisation of communities in the response to humanitarian crises ; taking stock of the implementation of the mission letter entrusted to her by the Head of State, reviewed its main lines, from strengthening mechanisms for monitoring and managing people in vulnerable situations, to a risk-management strategy adapted to the fragility of the economic fabric, the improvement of employment prospects for vulnerable groups, the promotion of community involvement, and the establishment of a framework for measuring results and evaluating performance ; explained that her department is drawing up an accountability and community engagement strategy to ensure that all emergency humanitarian and development actors align themselves with the State’s priorities ; added that her department is drawing up a ‘‘localisation strategy’’ aimed at strengthening the role and capacities of local actors, local NGOs, communities and authorities in the response to humanitarian crises, which allows the transfer of skills, capacity building and respect for the local context, and which ensures that humanitarian aid contributes to medium-, short- and long-term development ; “This strategy makes it possible to have a faster, more effective response that is better adapted to the needs of the community.”

a3689.speaker: Aïssa Laouan Wandarama, Nigerien Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management
a3689.name: Aïssa Laouan Wandarama
a3689.title: Nigerien Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management
a3689.speech: Noted that the national committee has been set up and that shortly the technical group must work in common agreement with the communities in order to gather their views on how they see the skills transferred ; “Normally at least 25% of the funds must go to the communities.”

a3838.speaker: Aaron Motsoaledi, South African Health Minister
a3838.name: Aaron Motsoaledi
a3838.title: South African Health Minister
a3838.speech: On Tuesday came on the Midday Report and was asked if he was still opposed to private educational institutions training medical doctors. "Yes," he replied, "extraordinarily so." His rationale is this: if there are private medical schools, then only the children of rich families will be able to become doctors; even if there is a complimentary system, where the private institutions help or work with the public institutions, eventually the good lecturers will leave the public sector and go to the private sector ; He also claims the real problem here is not that the private sector is not involved, it's that South Africa last built a new medical school twenty-nine years ago.

a3838.speaker: Wilmot James, DA Shadow Health Minister
a3838.name: Wilmot James
a3838.title: DA Shadow Health Minister
a3838.speech: While stressing his respect for Motsoaledi, says that when it comes to the private sector, "his intellectual doors seem to shut".

a3843.speaker: Government of Chad
a3843.name: Government of Chad
a3843.speech: Announced on 5 June 2025 the immediate suspension of the issuing of visas to American citizens, in direct response to the entry ban decreed the day before by President Donald Trump striking twelve nations including Chad, thus applying the principle of reciprocity.

a3843.speaker: White House
a3843.name: White House
a3843.speech: According to the White House, the measure targeting Chad is motivated by a "high rate of overstays, for 2022 and 2023" ; According to the White House, the measure could be lifted if the country puts in place technical and diplomatic reforms deemed satisfactory.

a3843.speaker: Government of Congo-Brazzaville
a3843.name: Government of Congo-Brazzaville
a3843.speech: Sees the measure as an injustice, to the point that it wonders whether the Trump administration has not made a mistake regarding Congo-Brazzaville.

a3843.speaker: Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno, President of Chad
a3843.name: Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno
a3843.title: President of Chad
a3843.speech: Used the terms of defending the country's sovereignty and dignity in justifying the reciprocal measure.

a3968.speaker: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama), as espoused by its president Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
a3968.name: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a3968.title: as espoused by its president Bertha Bangara-Chikadza
