a3968.speech: Called for urgent action to achieve fiscal discipline, export-led recovery and reform of foreign exchange markets to avert a deeper balance-of-payments crisis ; said Malawi will require a combination of monetary tightening to curb speculation and long-term investment in export growth to restore macroeconomic stability, cautioning that the widening trade gap is fuelling forex shortages, driving transactions underground and worsening inflationary pressures.

a3968.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) statement
a3968.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) statement
a3968.speech: Showed that Malawi's net international reserves (NIR) were projected to fall to negative $2.03 billion (about K3.55 trillion or 18.9 percent of gross domestic product) by the end of this year; projected that Malawi's net international reserves will deteriorate from –$1.02 billion in 2023 to –$2.03 billion in 2025.

a3968.speaker: Bloomberg (report)
a3968.name: Bloomberg (report)
a3968.speech: Reported that part of Malawi's external debt total includes almost $500 million owed to Africa Export and Import Bank (Afreximbank) and about $400 million with the Trade and Development Bank.

a3968.speaker: MacDonald Mafuta-Mwale, Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Governor
a3968.name: MacDonald Mafuta-Mwale
a3968.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Governor
a3968.speech: In February, barely a month in office, said the central bank had finalised the process of formulating measures aimed at crushing the parallel market foreign exchange supply as a key price stabilisation strategy.

a4070.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4070.name: Donald Trump
a4070.title: US President
a4070.speech: Restated his vision that “The Gaza Strip would be turned over to the United States by Israel at the conclusion of fighting,” while Palestinians would be temporarily resettled elsewhere.

a4070.speaker: UN, human rights groups and Arab leaders
a4070.name: UN
a4070.title: human rights groups and Arab leaders

a4070.speaker: Dragon TV (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: Dragon TV (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked: “There has been extensive opposition from the international community to U.S. President Trump's proposal to ‘clear out' and take over Gaza. What is China's comment?”

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On Gaza: “Gaza belongs to the Palestinian people. It is an inalienable part of the territory of Palestine, not a bargaining chip for political games, still less a prey of the strong. The war has already left Gaza in devastation and suffering. The international community, major countries in particular, should join hands to make Gaza better, rather than worse, by providing humanitarian assistance and helping with its reconstruction. China firmly supports the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people, believes that ‘the Palestinians governing Palestine' is an important principle that must be upheld in the post-conflict governance of Gaza, and opposes the forced displacement of the people of Gaza. China stands ready to work with the rest of the world for the realization of the two-State solution as the fundamental way forward, and for an early, just political settlement of the Palestinian question, namely, the establishment of an independent State of Palestine that enjoys full sovereignty based on the 1967 border and with east Jerusalem as its capital.”

a4070.speaker: AFP (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: AFP (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked whether China had a comment on the fact that “The U.S. said on Wednesday that its government vessels would sail for free through the Panama Canal following heavy pressure from President Donald Trump. But authorities at the waterway have swiftly issued a denial and said that no agreement had been reached.”

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On the Panama Canal: “On the Panama Canal issue, China made clear its position more than once. China, as always, respects Panama's sovereignty over the Canal and recognizes it as a permanently neutral international waterway. We respect the government of Panama's management and operation of the Canal. Never ever has China interfered.”

a4070.speaker: Le Monde (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: Le Monde (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked: “The new American President is making more and more controversial statements about Gaza, about Greenland, and about the Panama Canal. Do you think that's an opportunity for China to develop its influence?”

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On US policies and Chinese influence: “China will not comment on relevant U.S. policies. China, as always, develops its relations with other countries in accordance with the purposes and principles of the U.N. Charter. We also stand ready to contribute to world peace and development.”

a4070.speaker: Bloomberg (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: Bloomberg (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked the Foreign Ministry to confirm that “Mongolia's government is saying it plans to expand a railway connection with China to boost coal trade between the countries, and the deal will be finalized when the Mongolian Prime Minister visits China from February 13 to 15,” and whether the coal deal would be part of the agenda.

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On Mongolia: “China and Mongolia are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers. The two countries maintain close exchanges at various levels, and both sides are committed to enhancing connectivity and deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in various fields. As for the specific high-level exchange arrangement and cooperation you mentioned, we will release timely information if anything comes up. Please check back for updates.”

a4070.speaker: Yonhap News Agency (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: Yonhap News Agency (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked how China sees reports that some ROK government departments have blocked access to DeepSeek, following news about banning or restricting the use of DeepSeek in countries such as Italy, Australia, India, the U.S. and Japan.

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On DeepSeek restrictions: “I've noted this. Let me stress that the Chinese government attaches great importance to data privacy and security and protects it in accordance with the law. We have never asked and will never ask any company or individual to collect or store data against laws. China has all along opposed moves to overstretch the concept of national security or politicize trade and tech issues. We will firmly protect the lawful rights and interests of Chinese companies.”

a4070.speaker: Global Times (correspondent's question)
a4070.name: Global Times (correspondent's question)
a4070.speech: Asked for comment on “a handful of we-media accounts” that “recently posted groundless remarks that Cambodian leaders are choosing sides between China and the U.S. and that major cooperation projects between China and Cambodia are stalling.”

a4070.speaker: Guo Jiakun, Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.name: Guo Jiakun
a4070.title: Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson
a4070.speech: On Cambodia: “These remarks on Cambodia are purely groundless smears and deliberate vilification. China and Cambodia are iron-clad friends supporting each other and sharing weal and woe... China has remained Cambodia's biggest source of foreign investment and biggest trading partner for years running. Bilateral trade soared by nearly four times in the past decade. Cambodian leaders openly stressed more than once that China is Cambodia's most trusted friend... We firmly believe that the iron-clad friendship between China and Cambodia will steer clear of disruptions. We will not allow any deliberate vilification against our friendship and any rumor-monger shall bear legal responsibility and consequences.”

a4117.speaker: Mariam Fadiga, Executive Secretary of the State–Private Sector Consultation Committee (CCESP)
a4117.name: Mariam Fadiga
a4117.title: Executive Secretary of the State–Private Sector Consultation Committee (CCESP)
a4117.speech: said of the campaign launched on Thursday, November 14, 2024 in Abidjan: “it will last three weeks. (Then), we will hold the round table on December 6, 2024” ; According to Ms Mariam Fadiga, companies have requested projects or wished to support project promoters; for them it is a matter of seeing how to “contribute to the development of communities in support of the government’s Programme Côte d’Ivoire Solidaire.”

a4117.speaker: Mariam Doumbia, President of the NGO Jeunesse féminine active (JFA)
a4117.name: Mariam Doumbia
a4117.title: President of the NGO Jeunesse féminine active (JFA)
a4117.speech: presented the four flagship projects at the launch of the campaign: the first, she said, concerns “Espace filles” (Girls’ Space), which aims to create suitable hygiene facilities for girls in schools in order to reduce absenteeism due to menstrual poverty, benefiting 52,000 girls; the second is “Trajets sûrs” (Safe Journeys), aimed at making pupils’ travel safer by improving transport infrastructure and awareness-raising to reduce insecurity risks, targeting nearly 100,000 pupils; the third is “Réussir Ensemble” (Succeeding Together), aimed at adapting infrastructure and teaching resources for the inclusive education of children with disabilities, allowing 2,500 pupils to study in better conditions; the fourth, “SecurFood”, aims at the annual distribution of 250,000 nutritious meals to the most vulnerable pupils, improving their health, concentration and academic performance.

a4117.speaker: Sonia Shahrigian, Country Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4117.name: Sonia Shahrigian
a4117.title: Country Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4117.speech: made it known that the MCC’s objective, in supporting the institutional efforts of the Ivorian State, is for this approach to be sustainable with the involvement of stakeholders. The MCC has, in this dynamic, built neighbourhood secondary schools with Girls’ Spaces.

a4117.speaker: Dely Soumahoro, technical adviser representing the Ivorian Minister of Finance and Budget
a4117.name: Dely Soumahoro
a4117.title: technical adviser representing the Ivorian Minister of Finance and Budget
a4117.speech: declared that “the realisation of these projects will have a significant impact on the schooling of thousands of pupils” in Côte d’Ivoire, inviting companies to support the B4Gender project.

a4132.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4132.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4132.speech: Announced on Wednesday 16 April the immediate disbursement of 129 million dollars (around 78.5 billion CFA francs) to help Mali after the deadly floods of September and October 2024; according to the IMF, the floods caused considerable damage to infrastructure, devastated entire agricultural areas and compromised the livelihoods of thousands of families.

a4132.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4132.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a4132.speech: Demands reforms in return for the aid.

a4132.speaker: Malian authorities
a4132.name: Malian authorities
a4132.speech: Have committed to strengthening tax administration and broadening the tax base — measures to increase State revenue, indispensable to a sustainable economic recovery.

a4155.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (memo)
a4155.name: Marco Rubio
a4155.title: US Secretary of State (memo)
a4155.speech: Granted an “emergency humanitarian waiver” allowing PEPFAR to continue providing life-saving HIV medications to low-income countries, and approved an exemption for critical humanitarian efforts, including medical aid, food, and shelter assistance: “Implementers of existing life-saving humanitarian assistance programmes should continue or resume work if they have stopped, subject to the following directions. This resumption is temporary in nature, and except by separate waiver or as required to carry out this waiver, no new contracts shall be entered into.” ; Said this waiver does not apply to activities that involve abortions, family planning conferences, or administrative costs other than those covered: “Additional waivers or exceptions for humanitarian assistance not covered by this waiver may be sought through the Director of Foreign Assistance at the Department of State.”

a4155.speaker: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS (UNAIDS) (press statement)
a4155.name: Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS (UNAIDS) (press statement)
a4155.speech: Welcomes the decision by the US Secretary of State to continue life-saving HIV treatment.

a4155.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a4155.name: Winnie Byanyima
a4155.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS
a4155.speech: Said this decision recognises PEPFAR’s critical role in the global AIDS response and brings renewed hope to those affected by the disease: “UNAIDS welcomes this waiver from the US government which ensures that millions of people living with HIV can continue to receive life-saving HIV medication during the assessment of US foreign development assistance.” ; Said this urgent decision recognises PEPFAR’s critical role in the AIDS response and restores hope to people living with HIV.

a4155.speaker: US State Department fact sheet
a4155.name: US State Department fact sheet
a4155.speech: Showed that PEPFAR has saved the lives of an estimated 26 million people since its inception.

a4194.speaker: Greg Abbott, Texas Governor
a4194.name: Greg Abbott
a4194.title: Texas Governor
a4194.speech: highlighted concerns about data privacy and national security risks associated with these apps. Abbott stated, “Texas will not allow the Chinese Communist Party to infiltrate our state's critical infrastructure through data-harvesting AI and social media apps.”

a4194.speaker: Rep. Josh Gottheimer, US Congressman
a4194.name: Rep. Josh Gottheimer
a4194.title: US Congressman
a4194.speech: noted regarding proposed legislation banning DeepSeek federally: “This should be a no-brainer in terms of actions we should take immediately”.

a4383.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a4383.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.speech: Delivering the keynote address, described the invitation as both “historic and necessary,” highlighting the importance of full legislative integration into health fund administration ; “This isn’t just about numbers,” he said. “Health is not a donor issue. It is a national responsibility.”

a4383.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a4383.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.speech: Decried the opacity surrounding previous Global Fund interventions, criticising the lack of transparency from some recipients, including organisations with unverifiable addresses and those unwilling to submit to legislative scrutiny.

a4383.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a4383.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.speech: Directed particular criticism toward the HIV and malaria programme arms, accusing them of stonewalling parliament on key initiatives—most notably, a pending national survey on counterfeit malaria drugs ; praised the TB programme for consistent collaboration with the legislature and hailed progress made on the 2025 TB (Anti-Discrimination) Bill.

a4383.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a4383.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.speech: Called Nigeria’s $200 million commitment to health intervention following U.S. funding withdrawals a welcome but overdue development, and warned that such allocations must become the standard rather than an exception ; advocated for a permanent legislative seat on the CCM board, arguing that consistent parliamentary involvement would strengthen accountability and close critical coordination gaps.

a4383.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a4383.title: Chairman of the House Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria Control
a4383.speech: In closing remarks: “We cannot continue to underfund life-saving programmes and call ourselves responsible leaders,” he declared.

a4383.speaker: Mr Ayo Ipinmonye, First Vice-Chair, Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Nigeria
a4383.name: Mr Ayo Ipinmonye
a4383.title: First Vice-Chair, Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Nigeria
a4383.speech: Strongly advocated for a Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp) to optimise dwindling donor contributions ; with Nigeria’s Global Fund allocation recently reduced by 11 percent – from $970 million to $860 million – warned of dire consequences if disjointed funding practices and weak accountability persist ; issued a clarion call to the media to intensify investigative reporting and public education to maintain pressure on implementers and policymakers alike.

a4383.speaker: Dr Akinwunmi Fajola, Second Vice-Chair, Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Nigeria
a4383.name: Dr Akinwunmi Fajola
a4383.title: Second Vice-Chair, Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) Nigeria
a4383.speech: Presented sobering statistics – HIV prevalence has fallen from 5.8 percent to 1.3 percent, malaria rates have declined from 42 percent to 22 percent, and TB detection has surpassed 400,000 annually – but warned these were “fragile gains,” saying the risk of regression looms large unless Nigeria invests significantly in local health systems ; lamented the federal government’s minimal spending on health, which has remained at around 4–4.8 percent of the national budget—far below the Abuja Declaration’s 15 percent target ; reiterated that strong government backing is imperative for sustaining the CCM’s work and moving beyond aid dependency.

a4383.speaker: Dr Emperor Ubochioma, Global Fund TB Grant Unit
a4383.name: Dr Emperor Ubochioma
a4383.title: Global Fund TB Grant Unit
a4383.speech: Disclosed that Nigeria faces a 70 percent funding gap in its TB response—an estimated $700 million to $1 billion annually, and that without urgent intervention, essential services such as free TB diagnostics and treatment could collapse ; “The world is watching Nigeria,” he said. “We must lead from the front.”

a4383.speaker: Dr Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4383.name: Dr Temitope Ilori
a4383.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4383.speech: Framed the funding shortfalls as a transformative opportunity ; stressing the need for innovation and local ownership, challenged stakeholders to create a sustainable HIV response that can withstand global economic shocks.

a4383.speaker: Mr Ibrahim Tajudeen, Executive Secretary, CCM Nigeria
a4383.name: Mr Ibrahim Tajudeen
a4383.title: Executive Secretary, CCM Nigeria
a4383.speech: Rounded off the retreat with a firm call for institutional synergy, describing the gathering as a critical step in closing long-standing gaps in grant execution, particularly in the management of the ATM cluster ; emphasised the need to unlock national resources, define clear performance indicators, and embed inclusive and ethical governance in all health sector policies ; on the issue of transparency, affirmed that CCM’s structures already promote ethical standards and equal representation, but echoed Parliament’s position that legislative involvement must evolve from periodic observation to sustained inclusion, especially in policy alignment and disbursement procedures.

a4868.speaker: Alpha Daffae Senkpeni, Executive Director of Local Voices Liberia (LVL)
a4868.name: Alpha Daffae Senkpeni
a4868.title: Executive Director of Local Voices Liberia (LVL)
a4868.speech: Says it was not easy to fact-check fake news before iVerify, and explained that the tool has revolutionized fact-checking by ensuring speed and accuracy while previously relying on traditional media monitoring, which was challenging: "We had to manually follow various Facebook pages and newspapers. We assembled a team with a range of fact-checking skills, but with iVerify, we have been fact-checking, verifying videos, countering disinformation, and crucially, explaining complex stories to reveal the truth to the public."

a4868.speaker: Lien Bach, Chief of Party of USAID Internews Media Activity
a4868.name: Lien Bach
a4868.title: Chief of Party of USAID Internews Media Activity
a4868.speech: "The introduction of iVerify in Liberia was grounded in the idea of promoting responsible and factual dissemination of information. The tool provided robust verification and clarification of information during the elections."

a4868.speaker: Lenka Homolkova, former UNDP Chief Technical Advisor of the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP)
a4868.name: Lenka Homolkova
a4868.title: former UNDP Chief Technical Advisor of the Liberia Electoral Support Project (LESP)
a4868.speech: Commending the design of the tool, said, "iVerify was instrumental in addressing the challenges of misinformation and disinformation during the 2023 elections. This tool garnered increasing attention in elections and was recognized for contributing to election integrity both in Liberia and Sierra Leone. Content flagged as false by Local Voices was successfully removed from social media platforms, demonstrating the tool's effectiveness"; added that iVerify played a crucial role in combatting false information, as nobody wants to be associated with spreading misinformation, and said the flagged content removal significantly aided the 2023 general elections.

a4868.speaker: Anna Brzozowskwa, European Union in Liberia's Governance Team Lead
a4868.name: Anna Brzozowskwa
a4868.title: European Union in Liberia's Governance Team Lead
a4868.speech: Commends UNDP and LVL for the work done in fact-checking and developing the iVerify tool.

a4868.speaker: Nikolina Stalhand, Embassy of Sweden Program Officer for Democracy and Human Rights
a4868.name: Nikolina Stalhand
a4868.title: Embassy of Sweden Program Officer for Democracy and Human Rights
a4868.speech: Acclaiming the integrity of the tool, stated that many people around the world are applauding Liberia for successful elections held last year: "I think it is important to remember that this didn't just happen as an accident. Many people were involved in achieving this and the success of the elections was of course linked to combating misinformation and disinformation."

a5008.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) figures
a5008.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) figures
a5008.speech: Figures from the Reserve Bank of Malawi show average inflation slightly increased from 27.4 to 28.5 in the second quarter of 2025 due to maize price increase among other factors.

a5008.speaker: Chakudza Linje, RBM Director of Financial Markets
a5008.name: Chakudza Linje
a5008.title: RBM Director of Financial Markets
a5008.speech: In a presentation on Monday during the third Monetary Policy Forum in Mzuzu, attributed the increase to shortage of forex and high cost of production, and said RBM intends to bring together financiers and those who have bankable projects to increase production that will spike more exports and ensure availability of forex in the country: “We want to bring those who have investing capacity forward and see how they can be financed in ways that boost production.”

a5008.speaker: Chakudza Linje, RBM Director of Financial Markets
a5008.name: Chakudza Linje
a5008.title: RBM Director of Financial Markets
a5008.speech: Said that the decision [to maintain the policy rate at 26 percent] was based on risk considerations and is designed to achieve faster reduction in inflation rates.

a5008.speaker: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), Reserve Bank of Malawi
a5008.name: Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
a5008.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a5008.speech: The committee noted a decline in inflation from 30.7 percent in February to 27.1 percent in June 2025 as a key factor to arrive at the decision to maintain the policy rate at 26 percent.

a5008.speaker: Patrick Kuyokwa, forum participant
a5008.name: Patrick Kuyokwa
a5008.title: forum participant
a5008.speech: Said there is need for deliberate policies that will help reduce cost of production, and noted that when the general production is high in cost, the produce is minimal and prices are high depending on demand: “We are capable of producing enough but we have to lower our factors of production and produce at scale.”

a5046.speaker: Mohammed Kudus, Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.name: Mohammed Kudus
a5046.title: Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.speech: Called on his Ghana teammates, in an interview with Sports Illustrated, to approach the final hurdle of the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifiers with unwavering determination, stressing that qualifying is "non-negotiable" ; "We have to qualify at all costs. I think we are on the right path now."

a5046.speaker: Mohammed Kudus, Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.name: Mohammed Kudus
a5046.title: Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.speech: Admitted that the disappointment of missing out on the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations still weighs heavily on the squad and the nation, but said the team has shifted focus: "Not qualifying was a big disappointment, but I think the full focus now is on the World Cup qualifiers."

a5046.speaker: Mohammed Kudus, Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.name: Mohammed Kudus
a5046.title: Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.speech: "I think you represent your country like a one-time thing. That's the one with the biggest emotion and feeling for me. It means a lot wearing that jersey with a lot of pride."

a5046.speaker: Mohammed Kudus, Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.name: Mohammed Kudus
a5046.title: Black Stars midfielder (Tottenham Hotspur)
a5046.speech: Expressed his belief that the current generation can surpass Ghana's 2010 run: "2010 we went all the way to the quarterfinals. And I believe this squad can even do more than that. But first we have to qualify and then we can focus on the tournament itself."

a5275.speaker: Stakeholders in Zambia, including economists
a5275.name: Stakeholders in Zambia
a5275.title: including economists
a5275.speech: Have urged Zambia to take a measured approach in responding to calls for the realignment of the 2025 national budget following the recent decision by the U.S. government to freeze aid in some African countries; there have been calls from stakeholders in Zambia including economists to re-align the 2025 National Budget amid the foreign aid freeze.

a5275.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5275.name: Donald Trump
a5275.title: US President
a5275.speech: Announced the implementation of a 90-day freeze on foreign development assistance.

a5367.speaker: Lee Kuan Yew, late Prime Minister of Singapore (in his book From Third World To First World In One Generation)
a5367.name: Lee Kuan Yew
a5367.title: late Prime Minister of Singapore (in his book From Third World To First World In One Generation)
a5367.speech: "The world does not owe us a living. We cannot live by the begging bowl. A soft people will vote for people who promised a soft way out; when indeed, there is none" (p 53)

a5367.speaker: William Cobbett, 1762-1835 (VBQ p 194)
a5367.name: William Cobbett
a5367.title: 1762-1835 (VBQ p 194)
a5367.speech: "To be poor and independent is very nearly an impossibility."

a5367.speaker: Napoleon Bonaparte, 1769-1821
a5367.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
a5367.speech: "Impossible is a word to be found only in the dictionary of fools."

a5367.speaker: Global GDP per capita data
a5367.name: Global GDP per capita data
a5367.speech: Reveals that Singapore ranks with $39,370, US ranks number 6, with $86,601 and Nigeria, ranks 176 with a mere 5877.

a5367.speaker: Senate Ad Hoc Committee under Obasanjo (including late Senator Zwingina and Mrs Daisy Danjuma) — report
a5367.name: Senate Ad Hoc Committee under Obasanjo (including late Senator Zwingina and Mrs Daisy Danjuma) — report
a5367.speech: While investigating the mismanagement of funds belonging to Petroleum Development Trust Fund, PDTF, discovered improper payment of N250 million (N200 billion today) to a famous SAN. The report of the Ad Hoc Committee which discovered the fraud was swept under the carpet by the leaders of the National Assembly, NASS.

a5630.speaker: Nelson Mandela (quoted)
a5630.name: Nelson Mandela (quoted)
a5630.speech: "A vision without action is a dream. Action without vision is a waste of time. A vision followed by action can transform the world."

a5630.speaker: Collective of Muslim Associations of Mali (Mohamed Kimbiri, President)
a5630.name: Collective of Muslim Associations of Mali (Mohamed Kimbiri
a5630.title: President)
a5630.speech: Salutes this inspiring dynamic and calls on all African peoples to mobilise alongside the Kingdom of Morocco to make the causes of peace, justice and shared progress triumph.

a5683.speaker: Reports (unspecified)
a5683.name: Reports (unspecified)
a5683.speech: Reports indicate Somalia is keen to leverage Libya's expertise in oil exploration as Mogadishu begins allowing offshore petroleum surveys.

a5683.speaker: Governments of Libya and Somalia (joint agreements)
a5683.name: Governments of Libya and Somalia (joint agreements)
a5683.speech: Pledged to deepen cooperation on stability efforts, with Somalia using its temporary seat on the United Nations Security Council to advocate for regional peace initiatives, particularly in the Horn of Africa.

a5683.speaker: Somali and Libyan leaders
a5683.name: Somali and Libyan leaders
a5683.speech: Reportedly agreed to expedite the release and repatriation of Somali detainees held in Libyan prisons.

a5739.speaker: Human rights organizations and concerned people
a5739.name: Human rights organizations and concerned people
a5739.speech: Have raised serious outcry over the poisoned or expired food being distributed by Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri to flood victims.

a5739.speaker: Recipients of the relief items
a5739.name: Recipients of the relief items
a5739.speech: Claiming the products — packets of spaghetti and bags of rice — were already past their expiration dates beyond the consumption of human life.

a5739.speaker: Residents of Adamawa State
a5739.name: Residents of Adamawa State
a5739.speech: Describing the act as a grave betrayal of public trust by Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri.

a5739.speaker: Many beneficiaries (flood victims)
a5739.name: Many beneficiaries (flood victims)
a5739.speech: Expressed disappointment that a gesture meant to bring relief could potentially cause further harm and lead many to their untimely ends.

a5739.speaker: Experts
a5739.name: Experts
a5739.speech: Warn that consuming expired food carries significant health risks, including food poisoning, stomach infections, and other complications that could prove especially dangerous for vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly, and people with weakened immune systems.

a5739.speaker: Health officials
a5739.name: Health officials
a5739.speech: Are raising the dangers while the Governor himself is away in London.

a5739.speaker: Lawyers and civic rights groups
a5739.name: Lawyers and civic rights groups
a5739.speech: Say the incident could constitute a breach of the government’s duty of care to its citizens and might violate existing food safety and humanitarian assistance regulations.

a5739.speaker: People (residents/public)
a5739.name: People (residents/public)
a5739.speech: Are demanding that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, urgently unravel how deliberately the State Government procured poisoned and expired foodstuffs for people who lost their loved ones and properties in the massive flood.

a5821.speaker: Luc Deschamps, Honorary Consul of France
a5821.name: Luc Deschamps
a5821.title: Honorary Consul of France
a5821.speech: Said the support comes from "a nation which is courageously enduring a full-scale Russian invasion since February 24, 2022" ; "Before the war, Ukraine was a critical supplier for Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. Russian aggression has disrupted Ukrainian agriculture, causing ripple effects of food insecurity worldwide." ; "France, alongside the European Union, UN agencies, and partners across the global community, is acting to counter this severe crisis. Today’s delivery follows the pledge made by President Macron at the 2022 UN General Assembly — where France committed 14 million euros to support the mission of addressing the food crisis caused by the war in Ukraine." ; "It also aligns with the European initiative FARM and President Zelensky’s ‘Grain from Ukraine’ programme, demonstrating collective solidarity."

a5821.speaker: Per Lingarde, Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.name: Per Lingarde
a5821.title: Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.speech: Expressed his country’s high regard on how Ukraine "is able to defend its country against Russia’s ongoing aggression and at the same time contributes to the food supply on a global level" ; "We, the donors here present, support Ukraine’s efforts to export grain and other agricultural products to global markets and to the most vulnerable countries." ; "Global food insecurity is at record-high levels, exacerbated by climate change, conflicts and price shocks. This is felt here in Malawi and across the world and we follow with great concern the developments relating to the recent El Niño-induced drought and convey our deepest sympathies for the hardship caused to the Malawian people."

a5821.speaker: Per Lingarde, Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.name: Per Lingarde
a5821.title: Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.speech: Added that Sweden is a long time provider of development cooperation and humanitarian assistance, contributing to global food security and that they are proud to be one of WFP’s largest donors and to meeting acute food insecurity around the world ; "Since 2022, Sweden and other members of the European Union, have been at the forefront of global efforts to address the increased food insecurity and mitigate the consequences of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine." ; "This includes our work to support Ukrainian food exports reaching countries experiencing food insecurity. We are particularly proud to support the ‘Grain from Ukraine’ delivery to Malawi through WFP [as the] programme makes use of WFP’s strong logistics system to make sure that Ukrainian food production continues to reach those most in need of food assistance around the world." ; "With El Niño currently affecting Malawi and the region in an extraordinary manner, we are pleased to be able to support a strong and robust response, setting the stage for a recovery that is as swift as possible."

a5821.speaker: Per Lingarde, Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.name: Per Lingarde
a5821.title: Ambassador of Sweden to Zimbabwe and Malawi
a5821.speech: "Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine has from the start severely disrupted global agricultural production and trade, with dramatic consequences for vulnerable populations globally." ; "Russia has weaponised food by imposing an illegal blockade on Ukrainian seaports, as well as its destruction of Ukrainian agricultural infrastructure including ports, storage and export facilities." ; "Russia’s actions triggered an unprecedented peak in international food prices in 2022 and has led to volatile prices and disruption to food production and supplies." ; "These deplorable attacks on food supply chains continue and hungry people in many countries around the world have suffered as a result." ; emphasised that despite Russia’s war, "Ukraine remains committed to contribute to global food security by ensuring that its significant food production can reach global markets and therefore contribute to market stability".

a5821.speaker: Bouke Bjil, Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.name: Bouke Bjil
a5821.title: Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.speech: Said the Ukraine-Russia war should remind the world of the impacts of conflict and insecurity that "ripple out across the globe reaching people a world away from the frontlines" ; "Russia’s invasion of Ukraine exposed supply chain vulnerabilities, disrupting grain and fertilizer imports vital to Africa’s food security," he said. "This makes the need for peace even more urgent." ; "The Netherlands strongly condemns the Russian attack on Ukraine. For two years now, Ukraine has been defending itself every day against Russian aggression and The Netherlands will continue to support Ukraine as long as it takes." ; "And as a global partner in sustainable agriculture and climate action, we will continue to engage in initiatives that develop the necessary infrastructure and systems in Malawi, and Africa, to ensure security in the long run and inspite of a changing climate."

a5821.speaker: Bouke Bjil, Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.name: Bouke Bjil
a5821.title: Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.speech: Took cognizance that Malawi is living through difficult times as the country and the region reckon with the impacts of El Niño-intensified drought ; "For although we have welcomed some good rain recently, there is still a long road to the next harvest and 6 million Malawians remain in a precarious situation. For 900,000 of the worst affected people, the Grain from Ukraine initiative is going to make a difference." ; "Though this is a drop in the bucket against the needs, we must celebrate the positive impact of this contribution for so many Malawians. We are reminded today how, though separated by oceans and continents, we are connected."

a5821.speaker: Bouke Bjil, Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.name: Bouke Bjil
a5821.title: Honorary Consul for the Kingdom of The Netherlands
a5821.speech: Indicated that climate change is intensifying extreme weather events and that "all indications are that this drought was worsened by decades of greenhouse gas emissions, especially from wealthy, industrialised countries" ; "Climate justice demands that we address both the causes of climate change, together. This means that high-emitting nations must continue to cut emissions but also strengthen support to low-emitting countries that must adapt to climate impacts and quickly transition to low-carbon, clinate-resilient development pathways."

a5821.speaker: Andrii Pravednyk, Ambassador of Ukraine to Kenya and Malawi
a5821.name: Andrii Pravednyk
a5821.title: Ambassador of Ukraine to Kenya and Malawi
a5821.speech: Was very appreciative of the sentiments from his counterparts, saying despite Russia’s attempts to destroy their seaports and agricultural infrastructure, they are making sure they secure their export sea corridor to ensure a seamless transportation of grain globally ; "Let us continue to speak in one voice against this unprovoked and unjustified invasion of Ukraine," he said, adding that they were spurred to assist Malawi as both face challenges though of different proportions ; "We both were affected by CoVID-19 that hit the whole world but Malawi was hit with many unexpected shocks that include the two Cyclones, Ana and Freddy that displaced thousands of people, as well as the El Niño-induced drought."

a5909.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.name: Russell Dlamini
a5909.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.speech: Expressed his pleasure in receiving the new U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Marc Weinstock, describing him as a person who “radiates a pleasant personality and vibrant energy”; acknowledged the commendable work of Weinstock’s predecessor, Caitlin Piper, noting that she “worked well with the current Administration of the Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini and successfully strengthened the relations between the two countries”, and wished Piper success in her new assignment.

a5909.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.name: Russell Dlamini
a5909.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.speech: Emphasised that their discussions focused on “the opportunities that we can seize working together to serve our countries as well as to further strengthen our relations”, with key areas for collaboration including food security, border surveillance, and disaster risk management.

a5909.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.name: Russell Dlamini
a5909.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.speech: Touched on the recent reinstatement of critical health programs funded by USAID and PEPFAR, which are vital for HIV/AIDS prevention, care, and treatment in Eswatini, highlighting the importance of these programs in safeguarding public health, and noted the arrival of third-country migrants from the U.S.

a5909.speaker: Russell Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.name: Russell Dlamini
a5909.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a5909.speech: Described the United States as “one of the country’s most valuable diplomatic partners” and underscored that the relationship is “based on mutual trust and respect for one another”, reaffirming Eswatini’s commitment to deeper cooperation ; Addressed Weinstock directly: “To you, Chargé d’Affaires, seize the opportunity because time and chance have happened. Welcome to the Kingdom of Eswatini, the palace of Africa.”

a6224.speaker: Participants in the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience" (doctors and lawyers among the humanitarian workers)
a6224.name: Participants in the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience" (doctors and lawyers among the humanitarian workers)
a6224.speech: All are demanding dignity for their brothers in Gaza in particular and in Palestine in general.

a6224.speaker: International Criminal Court (ICC)
a6224.name: International Criminal Court (ICC)
a6224.speech: Issued arrest warrants against Israel's leaders, namely Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his former Defence Minister, Yoav Gallant, over the bombardments of the Gaza Strip.

a6224.speaker: Organisers of the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience"
a6224.name: Organisers of the "Maghreb Convoy of Resilience"
a6224.speech: Announce other humanitarian missions, whose conduct will depend on the success of the current convoy.

a6294.speaker: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6294.name: National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6294.speech: Announced that, despite the foreign currency shortage, there have been significant reforms in the financial sector.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE)
a6294.speech: Said that since he came to NBE there have been many changes. “About eight months ago our situation was very difficult. The reserve had significantly dropped and the situation regarding settling foreign debts was dire. We were at the edge of defaulting on our external loan settlements” ; “The coming of Abiy has led to new bilateral and multilateral partners who have provided hard currency. This will provide short term relief and enable us to think about further reform plans so that we can solve structural economic problems, hard currency earnings and exports” ; added that even though there have been delays in payments the government is now settling its loans properly, and providing hard currency to the manufacturing industry, although not as much as needed ; said the foreign reserve has also improved, but he declined to give a specific amount of available forex.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Said the economy was on the brink of a bad fate when the new government came in, but now things have improved; he expects the country's economy will register a similar rate as last year. “If we can provide what the manufacturing industry demands and the agriculture sector is able to meet its targets then economic growth will reach double digits” ; stated that the government is doing its best to provide foreign currency to the manufacturing sector but it is still less than they need, and amplified that the manufacturing sector also faces other problems like power and skilled labour.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: “We have worked on several things, and we are undergoing transitions, for instance in the past few months we have worked hard on remittances,” the governor said ; said the bank is improving the capacity of staff and establishing groups of experts from local and external professionals for applying several new businesses like bonds and capital markets in the financial sector, and that they are also working on a ten year roadmap.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Said the volume of loans in local banks has become quite high. “Due to the instability in the past few years some investors were unable to settle their debt properly so to do so, NBE has been working for extension of the loan settlement period with banks.”

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Said on suppliers' credit that local investors are supposed to be given priority but the foreign investors believed the country's law and they have also invested a huge sum so it would be bad if they are not able to make their products because of a hard currency shortage, which can affect the country's image. “It is not against the country's forex law,” Yinager said; for local investors, he added, “we are doing our best to help the manufacturing sector get hard currency via a letter of credit (LC).”

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Said he is informed about the selling of hard currency by exporters via banks that is illegal. “The basic problem is the shortage of foreign currency but to tackle illegal activities we are working our hardest and we are also meeting with banks' presidents to improve the financial sector. If we find someone involved in an illegal act in the foreign market, the actors and the bank will be punished,” he added ; “We have suspicions on illegality in hard currency allocation but have not been able to prove it and we will solve problems if we see any,” the governor explained.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: “Regarding first come first serve we have not gotten a better option than applying,” he said, regarding the allocation of foreign currency at banks ; “We are working with relevant body that gives licenses to the importers or exporters to solve the problem and identify the real market actors,” the governor said; he confirmed that there is a high burden at banks to provide foreign currency.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: On the growing loan interest rate: “Even though it is free for banks and a free market scheme, we shall see if it becomes a problem. But the issue will be answered after a relevant and adequate study,” Yinager said. “In this regard we have to speak with banks,” he added ; he said that banks, mainly private banks, are now providing loans without any challenge.

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Stated that loan approval from the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is not as much as is being requested. “The problem at DBE is very high in relation to debt given for investors mainly for those engaged in rain fed farms,” he said; agriculture loans amounting to 6.3 billion birr could be repossessed but NBE has ordered DBE to settle the matter legally. “We did not allow the birr or foreign currency that it wants until it normalizes non-performing loans,” the governor said ; the agriculture loans that DBE gave were taken purposely and in an organized network, according to Yinager: “Even though they received the loan legally, they took it in an organized manner even calculating how they will not settle the loan.”

a6294.speaker: Yinager Dessie, Governor of NBE
a6294.name: Yinager Dessie
a6294.title: Governor of NBE
a6294.speech: Said that in the coming year vast irrigation mainly in low land areas will be applied; said the manufacturing sector like textiles and agro processing is growing in the country which will be fed by local input. “The government has given serious attention to developing the agriculture sector to support the overall economy including solving the hard currency shortage,” he added; the governor has hinted that irrigation will be a priority for the coming budget year.

a6294.speaker: Ethiopian investors engaged in similar businesses
a6294.name: Ethiopian investors engaged in similar businesses
a6294.speech: Said the NBE suppliers' credit scheme, which is only allowed for foreign investors, created a problem.

a6294.speaker: Experts / legal experts
a6294.name: Experts / legal experts
a6294.speech: Are arguing that the directive goes against the investment proclamation amended in 2012; legal experts argued that the 769/2012 investment proclamation was erroneously mentioned in the central bank directive FXD/47/2017 as ‘679/2012’, and that its part one article 2/4 stated that investor means a domestic or a foreign investor that invests in Ethiopia.

a6294.speaker: A business consultant (anonymous)
a6294.name: A business consultant (anonymous)
a6294.speech: “The proclamation indicated that it has not divided local and foreign investors in relation to acquiring external loans,” a business consultant said, “but they claim the central bank directive goes against it.”

a6294.speaker: Bankers / bank officials (meeting with NBE leaders, November 2018)
a6294.name: Bankers / bank officials (meeting with NBE leaders
a6294.title: November 2018)
a6294.speech: Expressed their concern about the directive which they claim does not benefit banks or customers. They said illegal actors are still accessing the hard currency and distributing it unfairly ; in the past banks wanted the regulatory body to ease the new directive that controlled the way banks handle hard currency and asked the central bank to give them the responsibility of managing the LC process.

a6294.speaker: Central bank (NBE) leaders
a6294.name: Central bank (NBE) leaders
a6294.speech: Argued that they applied the directive to create fairness; NBE has told bankers to come up with a proposal to replace the directive.

a6294.speaker: Business actors and some bankers
a6294.name: Business actors and some bankers
a6294.speech: Told Capital that individuals who are not seeking hard currency for legitimate reasons lined up at banks to access foreign currency based on the directive, then sell their place in line to others.

a6294.speaker: Experts and the private sector / sector actors
a6294.name: Experts and the private sector / sector actors
a6294.speech: Expressed their concern regarding the growing loan interest at banks, which is about a quarter of the loan amount; the sector actors said that the interest rate has gone up to 25 percent on some types of loans, while the minimum rate which is mainly given to the export business is not small, according to experts in banks; they expressed their concern that it may have led to inflation and pressure borrowers into debt stress ; the private sector stated that loans particularly from state owned financial firms is lagging.

a6294.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6294.name: Abiy Ahmed
a6294.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a6294.speech: In his meeting with government leaders and prominent international businesspeople, he spoke about the support with irrigation development.

a6306.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Prime Minister of Senegal
a6306.name: Ousmane Sonko
a6306.title: Prime Minister of Senegal
a6306.speech: Confirmed the freeze of a crucial 500 million dollar financing from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC). "We cannot continue to depend on foreign aid," he declared, acknowledging the fragility of the situation.

a6306.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6306.name: Donald Trump
a6306.title: US President
a6306.speech: Is threatening to cut funding to South Africa in reaction to the land expropriation law.

a6306.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a6306.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a6306.title: President of South Africa
a6306.speech: Quickly defended the constitutionality of his approach, recalling that "we remain a democracy deeply rooted in the rule of law."

a6306.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a6306.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a6306.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a6306.speech: Says these decisions are part of a mercantilist strategy aimed at "optimising American spending" ; "The Trump administration had clearly shown its colours during Donald's first term by calling into question a great deal of spending and aid" ; "African countries did not anticipate Trump's return and his unilateral policy" ; says the suspension could have "harmful" consequences "even when the aid is restored."

a6306.speaker: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo, researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a6306.name: Dr Alioune Aboutalib Lo
a6306.title: researcher at the AKEM Centre in Istanbul
a6306.speech: "Another consequence would be the perception of the United States in Africa. China, its rival, has notably strengthened its image in certain African countries through its donations. Today, Trump's decisions risk not only tarnishing the image of the United States but also giving China the opportunity to show that it is much more credible than its rival on certain policies," he notes, stressing that "American interference policy is strengthening, with a militarisation of economic levers" ; he fears in particular reprisals against countries such as Senegal and Namibia, which have joined the Hague Group defending Palestinian rights.

a6387.speaker: Government of Liberia
a6387.name: Government of Liberia
a6387.speech: Has announced a policy reinforcing its austerity measures in the wake of US aid cuts; through the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning, has issued a strict directive to government spending entities to prioritize their priorities amid resource constraints.

a6387.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberian Finance Minister (memo of February 20, 2025 to Ministries, Agencies, and Commissions)
a6387.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6387.title: Liberian Finance Minister (memo of February 20, 2025 to Ministries, Agencies, and Commissions)
a6387.speech: “Scarcity of resources is a reality, and all Heads or Senior Management of Spending Entities must not lose sight of this reality. You're advised to prioritize the priorities,” the Minister stated ; has issued strict instructions for all government spending entities to adhere to their approved budgets for Fiscal Year 2025 and to exercise fiscal prudence in what it describes as a “challenging fiscal environment” ; “Please manage your budget well. Your budget is for the entire 12 months of 2025. So, you're strongly advised not to execute your budget as if it were a six-month or one-quarter budget” ; further said that all spending entities will likely not receive any supplemental resources from the government if they exhaust their budget lines early.

a6387.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.name: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.speech: Informed government institutions that the budget is a projection until revenue is actually raised through the efforts, dedication, integrity, and sacrifice of the Liberia Revenue Authority, the MFDP, and all other stakeholders involved in revenue generation ; explained, “This year's budget is US$880.7 million, reflecting a growth of 19.2% over last year's Recast Budget of US$738.9 million. While this US$141.8 million increase is undeniably impressive, it is still far below the upwards of US$2 billion in funding requests for 2025 that the MFDP received from spending entities during the formulation of the current budget.”

a6387.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.name: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.speech: Informed senior management of spending entities that, with the country now in the second month of the Fiscal 2025 National Budget, it has been receiving a large number of requests for additional funds from spending entities to address new priorities and spending pressures that were not included in their budgets ; stated, “The first source to fund an unforeseen demand or priority that arises during budget execution should be the budget of the spending entity itself.” ; reminded all spending entities that only US$3.26 million was approved as a contingency reserve fund in the Fiscal Year 2025 budget, the only source of unallocated funds from which the Ministry can obtain additional funds ; added, “This amount is obviously minuscule compared to the sheer number of legitimate unforeseen spending pressures that arise during the course of the year. What this simply means is that the MFDP, operating within the structures of the Public Financial Management and Budget Transfer laws, must make the difficult decision of looking to other budgeted appropriations to fund legitimate unforeseen spending demands.”

a6387.speaker: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.name: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia (memo)
a6387.speech: Concluded by emphasizing that the cooperation of all spending entities is critical to ensuring the efficient, impactful, and equitable execution of the national budget.

a6490.speaker: Jean Sendeza, Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare of Malawi
a6490.name: Jean Sendeza
a6490.title: Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare of Malawi
a6490.speech: Has commended the 314 graduates from Magomero Community Development College for their dedication to improving the lives of Malawian children and vulnerable communities, describing them as key partners in driving Malawi's human capital development agenda; applauded the students who benefited from scholarship programmes funded by the World Bank, UNESCO, USAID and the British Council and emphasised the importance of their work in complementing government efforts: “We expect you to deliver integrated early childhood development services, protect vulnerable children, and contribute to national development. Your roles are essential not only to national policy goals but also to broader regional initiatives such as the African Union’s Agenda 2063.”

a6490.speaker: Jean Sendeza, Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare of Malawi
a6490.name: Jean Sendeza
a6490.title: Minister of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare of Malawi
a6490.speech: Recognised the graduates’ critical role in strengthening community initiatives such as nutrition education in Community-Based Childcare Centres (CBCCs) and schools, caregiver support, and child protection services, and urged them to enhance community-level programmes, including care groups and school meal schemes: “I urge all of you to serve with dedication and professionalism. The country is counting on you.”

a6490.speaker: Thokozani Mtapawonga, Principal of Magomero Community Development College
a6490.name: Thokozani Mtapawonga
a6490.title: Principal of Magomero Community Development College
a6490.speech: Described the graduation as a landmark achievement for the college and an important step towards Malawi’s long-term development vision: “This ceremony marks not only the completion of your training but also the start of your service to the nation as passionate and skilled professionals. We take pride in your contribution to Malawi’s Agenda 2063.” She further emphasised that the graduates are well-equipped to make a meaningful impact in sectors that directly support community development.

a6550.speaker: Emanuela Del Re, Special Representative of the European Union for the Sahel
a6550.name: Emanuela Del Re
a6550.title: Special Representative of the European Union for the Sahel
a6550.speech: "We remain alongside the Burkinabe with development cooperation and humanitarian aid projects that are essential for the population. I appreciate the terms of cooperation between my institution and Burkina Faso, and we intend to strengthen our collaboration for the well-being of the population." ; Listing prospective areas of cooperation in agriculture, education and sanitation, she specified that relations between Burkina Faso and the European Union remain always based on mutual trust ; The visit was an opportunity for the Special Representative to reassure the Burkinabe government of the EU's commitment alongside the people and the authorities of the country.

a6550.speaker: Burkinabe governmental delegation (Minister of State for Defence Kassoum Coulibaly and Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation Stella Eldine Kabre/Kabore)
a6550.name: Burkinabe governmental delegation (Minister of State for Defence Kassoum Coulibaly and Minister Delegate for Regional Cooperation Stella Eldine Kabre/Kabore)
a6550.speech: Expressed its gratitude to the EU for its support and presented to Mrs. Del Re the progress achieved, thanks also to the mobilisation of the Burkinabe who subscribe to the vision of the President of Faso, Head of State ; The ministers cited, among other things, the reconquest of approximately 71% of the territory, the release of hostages both military and civilian, including the two lawyers recently kidnapped by terrorists, the mobile clinics initiative across Burkina Faso, the distribution of tractors in support of the agricultural sector, and the recent holding of major events such as SIAO and the Tour du Faso.

a6550.speaker: Members of the Burkinabe government
a6550.name: Members of the Burkinabe government
a6550.speech: Note with regret that Burkina Faso continues to be the victim of manipulation and disinformation on the part of certain Western media outlets ; They reassured the EU Representative for the Sahel of the government's readiness always to provide true information to partners on all subjects falling within the field of cooperation between Burkina Faso and the European Union.

a6577.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (new report)
a6577.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (new report)
a6577.speech: Reveals that the majority of people who lose their lives while migrating do not do so by choice, but out of sheer desperation, fleeing insecurity, conflict, natural disasters and other humanitarian crises that make life untenable in their country of origin ; reports that since 2014 more than 52,000 people have died trying to escape countries affected by crises, nearly 72% of all migrant deaths recorded worldwide over that period, with more than 39,000 dying within crisis zones themselves and more than 13,500 while trying to flee conflicts or disasters ; highlights that more than half of the migrant deaths recorded since 2014 occurred in or near countries struck by conflict or disaster, with more than 5,000 dying in transit in Afghanistan, notably after the political upheaval of 2021, more than 3,100 Rohingya from Myanmar dying often in shipwrecks or while trying to cross into Bangladesh, and the central Mediterranean remaining the deadliest migration route in the world with nearly 25,000 people missing at sea ; notes that migrants are still too often forgotten in humanitarian response plans, with needs assessments and humanitarian appeals not taking sufficient account of populations on the move even though one missing migrant in four comes from a country in a crisis situation.

a6577.speaker: Amy Pope, Director General of the International Organization for Migration
a6577.name: Amy Pope
a6577.title: Director General of the International Organization for Migration
a6577.speech: Says these figures are a painful reminder that human beings put their lives in danger when insecurity, the absence of opportunities and other factors deprive them of any safe option to remain at home ; calls for sustained investment to foster stability and prospects in communities of origin, so that migration becomes a voluntary choice and not an obligation ; stresses the importance of building together safe, legal and orderly migration pathways in order to protect human lives when staying is no longer possible.

a6577.speaker: Julia Black, coordinator of the "Missing Migrants" project and author of the report
a6577.name: Julia Black
a6577.title: coordinator of the "Missing Migrants" project and author of the report
a6577.speech: Recalls that many migrants fall into oblivion, all the more so as the lack of data, particularly in war or disaster zones, prevents an accurate picture of the real number of deaths.

a6577.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a6577.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a6577.speech: Is making an urgent appeal to States and humanitarian partners to join their efforts to ensure that migrants are no longer excluded from crisis responses, which means opening legal migration pathways, better access to aid and health care, as well as investment in data systems capable of better tracking and protecting people at risk.

a6700.speaker: Activists such as Ahmed Assid
a6700.name: Activists such as Ahmed Assid
a6700.speech: Highlight the slow disappearance of the Amazigh language, even though it is regarded as the living heart of Amazigh identity.

a6706.speaker: Ashraf Ghani, President of Afghanistan
a6706.name: Ashraf Ghani
a6706.title: President of Afghanistan
a6706.speech: Was widely quoted saying he left Afghanistan to avoid bloodshed.

a6706.speaker: Esther Davinia Anyakun, Uganda's state minister for relief, disaster preparedness and refugees
a6706.name: Esther Davinia Anyakun
a6706.title: Uganda's state minister for relief, disaster preparedness and refugees
a6706.speech: Broke the news that America had requested Uganda to host 2,000 of the fleeing Afghans; said President Yoweri Museveni had ordered her to make preparations to host 2,000 refugees from Afghanistan who would be brought in shifts of 500; revealed that the UNHCR had secured the Imperial Group of hotels in Entebbe as a transit centre for the Afghans to arrive at and be screened; said the Afghans are expected to stay in Uganda for at least three months before being relocated to a third country.

a6706.speaker: Elijah Okeyo, IRC Uganda Country Director
a6706.name: Elijah Okeyo
a6706.title: IRC Uganda Country Director
a6706.speech: "The IRC is proud to be complementing the efforts of the Government of Uganda and US embassy to receive and support 51 Afghan evacuees that arrived in Uganda at 7.53am this morning." ; "The evacuees from Afghanistan will stay temporarily in Uganda whilst in transit whilst applying for asylum to countries of resettlement such as the US." ; "Uganda has a long history and tradition of welcoming refugees from all over the world and is one of the world's largest refugee hosting countries, with 1.5 million refugees mainly from South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo."

a6706.speaker: Uganda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6706.name: Uganda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a6706.speech: Said the evacuees who included men, women and children underwent the necessary security screening as well as the mandatory COVID-19 testing and the required quarantine procedures.

a6706.speaker: American embassy in Kampala (statement)
a6706.name: American embassy in Kampala (statement)
a6706.speech: Noted that as the largest bilateral supporter of refugees in Uganda and their Ugandan host communities, the United States appreciates the Ugandan people for their generosity and hospitality toward these communities ; "The Government of Uganda has once again demonstrated a willingness to play its part in matters of international concern. We commend its efforts and those of the local and international organizations in Uganda who are providing humanitarian support in partnership with the Government of Uganda for these evacuees from Afghanistan."

a6706.speaker: Spokesperson of the US mission in Kampala
a6706.name: Spokesperson of the US mission in Kampala
a6706.speech: "The United States appreciates the Government of Uganda's offer to provide temporary assistance to Afghanistan evacuees and commends international organization representatives in Uganda for their partnership and for lending their expertise and support to Afghanistan evacuees."

a6884.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO) (first bulletin on “The impact of the Israel-Hamas conflict on the labour market and livelihoods in the occupied Palestinian territory”, published 6 November)
a6884.name: International Labour Organization (ILO) (first bulletin on “The impact of the Israel-Hamas conflict on the labour market and livelihoods in the occupied Palestinian territory”
a6884.title: published 6 November)
a6884.speech: According to the ILO, at least 61% of jobs have been lost in the Gaza Strip since the start of the fighting between Israel and Hamas; the West Bank is also affected with a loss of about 24% of jobs; the total number of jobs lost in the two areas making up the occupied Palestinian Territories is estimated at 390,000, translating into daily labour income losses of $16 million. At least 182,000 jobs (61%) have been lost in the Gaza Strip since the start of the war; in the West Bank the loss is estimated at 208,000 jobs (24%) over the same period (7 to 31 October 2023). The publication indicates that the conflict has serious repercussions not only on the labour market and employment prospects but also on livelihoods throughout the occupied Palestinian Territories ; the bulletin stresses that entire neighbourhoods of Gaza have been destroyed, infrastructure has been severely damaged, businesses have closed, large-scale internal displacement has occurred, and the lack of water, food and fuel is paralysing economic activity.

a6884.speaker: ILO labour force survey (second quarter of 2023)
a6884.name: ILO labour force survey (second quarter of 2023)
a6884.speech: According to the survey, the unemployment rate in Gaza reached 46.4% (66.2% for women and 40.5% for men).

a6884.speaker: Ruba Jaradat, ILO Regional Director for Arab States
a6884.name: Ruba Jaradat
a6884.title: ILO Regional Director for Arab States
a6884.speech: Declared that “the ongoing hostilities do not represent only an enormous humanitarian crisis in terms of loss of human life and basic human needs, they also represent a social and economic crisis that has caused enormous damage to jobs and businesses, with repercussions that will be felt for many years to come” ; specified that in the long term the ILO would help workers “to recover jobs by associating them with social protection initiatives, to the full extent of our mandate”.

a6884.speaker: ILO Governing Body
a6884.name: ILO Governing Body
a6884.speech: Issued a call, in accordance with international humanitarian law, for rapid and safe humanitarian access to allow the delivery of humanitarian aid to civilians throughout the Gaza Strip.

a6884.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO)
a6884.name: International Labour Organization (ILO)
a6884.speech: Has prepared a three-phase response programme to address the impact of the crisis on the labour market and on Palestinian livelihoods: a first, already-ongoing relief phase providing immediate assistance to Palestinian workers, notably through emergency livelihood support programmes, essentially for Gaza residents who lost employment in Israel and are stranded in the West Bank; a second review phase of data collection and impact analysis to help plan, prioritise and refine interventions; and a final phase focused on job creation. A meeting organised by the ILO will be held on 9 November to raise $20 million to finance an aid programme.

a6991.speaker: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM)
a6991.name: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM)
a6991.speech: Promises to build houses for young people, jobs and an increase in the subsidy for the elderly.

a6991.speaker: Lutero Simango, MDM presidential candidate
a6991.name: Lutero Simango
a6991.title: MDM presidential candidate
a6991.speech: Promises to raise the elderly subsidy from the current 600 to 1,200 meticais and to mobilise investors to build small units for processing and preserving fresh produce - promises made this Monday to the population of Nhamatanda district, Sofala province.

a6991.speaker: Daniel Chapo, Frelimo presidential candidate
a6991.name: Daniel Chapo
a6991.title: Frelimo presidential candidate
a6991.speech: Promises the establishment of farms in Maringúe to capitalise on the district's agricultural potential and generate employment ; in Gorongosa, Sofala, promised to build a peace monument, an operating theatre at the local hospital and secondary schools for young people.

a6991.speaker: Renamo (in Maputo City)
a6991.name: Renamo (in Maputo City)
a6991.speech: Promises to build decent schools and to pay maintenance pensions for the elderly, should Issufo Momade win the elections.

a6991.speaker: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM), campaigning in Laulane, Kamavota Municipal District, Maputo City
a6991.name: Mozambique Democratic Movement (MDM)
a6991.title: campaigning in Laulane, Kamavota Municipal District, Maputo City
a6991.speech: Promised jobs for young people and an improvement in the quality of education in the country, should it win the 9 October elections.

a6991.speaker: Joaquim Chissano, former President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6991.name: Joaquim Chissano
a6991.title: former President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6991.speech: Says that all vital forces must be guided by tolerance and serenity in the ongoing electoral process ; welcomed the order and calm that have characterised the election campaign so far.

a6991.speaker: Maputo City Council
a6991.name: Maputo City Council
a6991.speech: Promises to change the situation in which around five thousand stalls stand empty in the city's municipal markets while hundreds of people trade on the pavements around them.

a7163.speaker: African Action Congress (AAC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.name: African Action Congress (AAC)
a7163.title: Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.speech: Condemned the recent demolition of residential homes in Karsana, Abuja, describing the exercise as a “brutal, inhumane and state-backed assault on the poor”; condemned the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) under the leadership of Minister Nyesom Wike, accusing it of carrying out the demolitions with the support of armed police, without due process or consideration for the human rights of residents. “This brazen act of violence, carried out with the backing of armed police, is a stark reminder of the callous disregard for human life and dignity that pervades our society. The circumstances surrounding this demolition are shrouded in controversy, with allegations of corrupt dealings, blatant disregard for due process, and a clear disregard for the rights and dignity of the affected citizens. It is unconscionable that in a society that prides itself on being civilized, such brutal and inhumane actions can be perpetrated against vulnerable citizens, including women, children, and the elderly.” ; According to the AAC, allegations of corruption and irregular land dealings are swirling around the demolition, with many victims claiming they were never served prior notices or given alternatives.

a7163.speaker: African Action Congress (AAC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.name: African Action Congress (AAC)
a7163.title: Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.speech: Demanded that the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, immediately ensure “fair and adequate compensation” to all affected families, along with the provision of alternative housing: “We condemn in the strongest possible terms the wanton destruction of property and the displacement of innocent citizens. The FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, must take immediate action to address this egregious situation. We demand that the minister: Ensure fair and adequate compensation to all affected families, taking into account the trauma and hardship they have endured. The compensation must be prompt, just, and sufficient to enable the families to rebuild their lives.” ; Called on Wike to provide alternative housing for the displaced families and prevent further suffering and hardship, noting that the government has a responsibility to protect its citizens and ensure they have access to basic necessities, such as shelter.

a7163.speaker: African Action Congress (AAC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.name: African Action Congress (AAC)
a7163.title: Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.speech: “Furthermore, we call on the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Alleviation to provide immediate humanitarian assistance to the affected families, including shelter, food, and other essential necessities. The historical context of the Karsana community cannot be ignored; the very name of the community is a testament to the decades-long existence of its inhabitants, long before this administration's tenure. It is imperative that any development agenda prioritises the rights and dignity of the people, guided by due process and the rule of law. Development without people is meaningless; thus, we emphasise that the welfare of citizens must be paramount in any development initiative.”

a7163.speaker: African Action Congress (AAC), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.name: African Action Congress (AAC)
