a7163.title: Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chapter (statement signed by its Chairman, Agena Robert Ande)
a7163.speech: The party vowed to continue mobilising and speaking against the “systematic displacement and impoverishment” of the poor by state institutions, and ended the statement with a warning to the government that ‘enough is enough’: “It is time to prioritise the welfare and dignity of citizens over the interests of powerful individuals and corporations. It is time to uphold the law and protect the rights of all citizens, regardless of their social status or location.”

a7163.speaker: Christopher Maikalangu, Chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC)
a7163.name: Christopher Maikalangu
a7163.title: Chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC)
a7163.speech: Inspected the demolition site in Abuja and alleged that the demolitions were carried out by a private developer, Oceanic Properties and Equilibrium Concept; condemned the developer’s actions, describing them as a grave injustice against the community, and vowed to pursue legal redress on behalf of the affected residents; said the affected individuals are legitimate indigenous Gbagyi people of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and are entitled to full compensation for the damages inflicted upon them.

a7163.speaker: Christopher Maikalangu, Chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC)
a7163.name: Christopher Maikalangu
a7163.title: Chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC)
a7163.speech: Appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, for immediate intervention to address the situation; also appealed to the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Alleviation to intervene in their immediate resettlement, adding that many families had been rendered homeless.

a7306.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (stop-work order)
a7306.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (stop-work order)
a7306.speech: In January 2025, USAID issued a sudden stop-work order to all its aid recipients in Namibia; the directive demanded an immediate halt to all USAID-funded activities, including those at the heart of the DREAMS initiative, pending a 90-day policy review.

a7306.speaker: Selma Amukwaya (22), former DREAMS participant
a7306.name: Selma Amukwaya (22)
a7306.title: former DREAMS participant
a7306.speech: "I was lost before DREAMS. I did not know much about my body, HIV prevention or how to even think for myself" ; "Now, it's gone. We don't even know why. No one told us anything."

a7306.speaker: Tuli Kamati (20), former DREAMS participant
a7306.name: Tuli Kamati (20)
a7306.title: former DREAMS participant
a7306.speech: "I learned how to make soap, budget money, and how to say no to unsafe sex. It gave us strength and dignity."

a7306.speaker: Former DREAMS mentor (anonymous, asked not to be named)
a7306.name: Former DREAMS mentor (anonymous
a7306.title: asked not to be named)
a7306.speech: "Girls just came one day, and the doors were closed" ; "We did not even get to explain. Some of the girls cried. They thought they did something wrong."

a7306.speaker: Namibian Ministry of Health and Social Services
a7306.name: Namibian Ministry of Health and Social Services
a7306.speech: Has acknowledged the disruption, expressing a desire to sustain services for adolescent girls and young women; however, resources are scarce.

a7306.speaker: Selma Amukwaya (22), former DREAMS participant
a7306.name: Selma Amukwaya (22)
a7306.title: former DREAMS participant
a7306.speech: "Even if they don't bring DREAMS back, they must not forget us. We are still here. We are still dreaming."

a7425.speaker: Shiferaw Teklemariam (PhD), head of the Disaster Risk Management Commission (DRMC)
a7425.name: Shiferaw Teklemariam (PhD)
a7425.title: head of the Disaster Risk Management Commission (DRMC)
a7425.speech: Appearing before members of Parliament’s Standing Committee for International Relations & Peace Affairs, defended the bill as a means of preserving “dignity, independence and sovereignty.”

a7425.speaker: Federal legislators (members of Parliament’s Standing Committee for International Relations & Peace Affairs)
a7425.name: Federal legislators (members of Parliament’s Standing Committee for International Relations & Peace Affairs)
a7425.speech: Summoned Shiferaw Teklemariam to explain the new bill and questioned why a new federal bureaucracy should be layered atop existing agencies rather than streamline and reinforce them.

a7425.speaker: Climate models
a7425.name: Climate models
a7425.speech: Warn that, without adaptation, Ethiopia could lose up to seven percent of its agricultural output by 2030.

a7425.speaker: Donors
a7425.name: Donors
a7425.speech: Trimmed pledges by 450 million dollars in 2024, citing crises from Gaza to Ukraine.

a7425.speaker: Federal officials / policymakers
a7425.name: Federal officials / policymakers
a7425.speech: Hope to raise close to 10 billion Br annually, a tenfold increase on current domestic outlays ; warn that the alternative is far costlier.

a7425.speaker: Sceptics
a7425.name: Sceptics
a7425.speech: Warn citizens already squeezed by double-digit inflation may baulk at fresh deductions.

a7425.speaker: Government’s first Risk Financing Strategy (2023-2030)
a7425.name: Government’s first Risk Financing Strategy (2023-2030)
a7425.speech: Nods to such instruments as parametric insurance and securitisation but lacks concrete deadlines for implementation; the new strategy plans to substitute improvisation with insurance.
